In IELTS essays it is a precise alternative to "become worse"; WORSEN is a slightly less formal synonym that can also be transitive.

lessons.unit: Advanced academic vocabulary: action and description

expressions.usage: dialogue = a formal discussion between two groups
integration = becoming a full member of a group or society
exchange = giving one thing and receiving another
transfer = moving something from one place to another
transition = the process of changing from one state to another
collaboration = working with others to produce something
participation = taking part in an activity
decision-making = the process of deciding something important

sentences.en: The new software facilitates the exchange of information between departments.
sentences.az: Yeni proqram şöbələr arasında məlumat mübadiləsini asanlaşdırır.

sentences.en: The teacher's role is to facilitate learning, not to give lectures.
sentences.az: Müəllimin rolu mühazirə oxumaq deyil, öyrənməyə şərait yaratmaqdır.

sentences.en: The agreement will facilitate the transition to a market economy.
sentences.az: Saziş bazar iqtisadiyyatına keçidi asanlaşdıracaq.

sentences.en: Online tools facilitate collaboration between researchers in different countries.
sentences.az: Onlayn alətlər müxtəlif ölkələrdəki tədqiqatçıların birgə işini asanlaşdırır.

usage: FACILITATE means to make an action or process easier or more likely to happen. Its object is a process, not a person: "facilitate communication" – not "facilitate students". It is formal and very common in academic and business English, where it replaces "help" or "make easier". A FACILITATOR is a person who helps a group to work together and reach decisions without taking sides.

lessons.unit: Advanced academic vocabulary: action and description

expressions.usage: wildly = in an extreme and uncontrolled way
fluctuate BETWEEN A and B
unpredictably = in a way that cannot be known in advance
currency = the money used in a particular country
seasonal = happening during a particular season
minor = small and not very important
mood = the way you feel at a particular time

expressions.az: dəyişkən tale (uğurun gah gülüb, gah dönməsi)
expressions.usage: fortune = luck; the good and bad things that happen

sentences.en: Oil prices have fluctuated wildly in recent months.
sentences.az: Son aylarda neft qiymətləri kəskin şəkildə enib-qalxıb.

sentences.en: The temperature fluctuates between 20 and 30 degrees in summer.
sentences.az: Yayda temperatur 20 ilə 30 dərəcə arasında dəyişir.

sentences.en: The number of visitors shows clear seasonal fluctuations.
sentences.az: Ziyarətçilərin sayında aydın mövsümi dəyişmələr müşahidə olunur.

sentences.en: Apart from minor fluctuations, sales remained stable throughout the year.
sentences.az: Cüzi dəyişmələr istisna olmaqla, satışlar il boyu sabit qaldı.

usage: FLUCTUATE means to change frequently in size, amount or level, especially from one extreme to another. It is intransitive and is one of the key verbs for describing graphs in IELTS Writing Task 1, together with RISE, FALL, PEAK and LEVEL OFF. Patterns: fluctuate BETWEEN x AND y; fluctuate AROUND a figure; fluctuations IN something. Typical adverbs: wildly, widely, considerably, slightly.

expressions.usage: recommendation = an official suggestion about the best thing to do
legislation = a law or set of laws
directive = an official instruction
sanction = an official action taken against a country to force it to obey
initiative = a new plan for dealing with a problem
procedure = the official or correct way of doing something
guideline = official advice about how to do something
oversee = watch a process to make sure it is done correctly

sentences.en: The government has promised to implement the committee's recommendations in full.
sentences.az: Hökumət komitənin tövsiyələrini tam şəkildə həyata keçirməyə söz verib.

sentences.en: The new safety procedures will be implemented next month.
sentences.az: Yeni təhlükəsizlik prosedurları gələn ay tətbiq olunacaq.

sentences.en: A special team was set up to oversee the implementation of the reforms.
sentences.az: İslahatların icrasına nəzarət etmək üçün xüsusi qrup yaradıldı.

sentences.en: The plan is good in theory, but it will be difficult to implement.
sentences.az: Plan nəzəri cəhətdən yaxşıdır, amma onu həyata keçirmək çətin olacaq.

usage: IMPLEMENT means to put a decision, plan or law into action; you decide first and implement afterwards. It is the standard formal verb with policy, plan, strategy, reform, measure and recommendation. Compare CARRY OUT (neutral), ENFORCE (make people obey a law) and EXECUTE (formal: perform a plan or order). As a noun, an IMPLEMENT is a simple tool: farming implements. The verb ends in /ment/, the noun in a weak /mənt/.

expressions.usage: incentive + to-infinitive
ample = more than enough
perverse = having an effect opposite to the one intended
bonus = extra money added to your pay
lucrative = producing a lot of money
fiscal = connected with government money, especially taxes
recycle = treat used things so that they can be used again
disincentive TO work / TO investment

sentences.en: Low wages give people little incentive to work harder.
sentences.az: Aşağı maaşlar insanlara daha çox işləmək üçün az stimul verir.

sentences.en: The government offers fiscal incentives to companies that invest in poorer regions.
sentences.az: Hökumət yoxsul regionlara sərmayə qoyan şirkətlərə vergi güzəştləri təklif edir.

sentences.en: The tax break gives firms ample incentive to hire young people.
sentences.az: Vergi güzəşti şirkətlərə gəncləri işə götürmək üçün kifayət qədər stimul verir.

sentences.en: High taxes can act as a disincentive to investment.
sentences.az: Yüksək vergilər sərmayə qoyuluşuna həvəsi azalda bilər.

usage: An INCENTIVE is something that encourages you to do something, usually a reward such as money. It is followed by TO + infinitive ("an incentive to save") or FOR ("incentives for employers"). A PERVERSE INCENTIVE is a term from economics for a reward that produces the opposite of the intended result. MOTIVATION comes from inside a person; an INCENTIVE is offered from outside. Verb: INCENTIVISE somebody TO do something.

expressions.usage: The preposition is IN: the risks inherent in the plan
contradiction = a difference between two statements that cannot both be true
bias = an unfair preference for one side
characteristic = a typical feature or quality
defect = a fault in the way something is made
evil = morally very bad
superior = better than others
subjective = based on personal opinions rather than facts

sentences.en: There are risks inherent in any investment.
sentences.az: İstənilən sərmayə qoyuluşuna xas olan risklər var.

sentences.en: There is an inherent contradiction in the government's policy.
sentences.az: Hökumətin siyasətində daxili ziddiyyət var.

sentences.en: No language is inherently superior to another.
sentences.az: Heç bir dil mahiyyətcə digərindən üstün deyil.

sentences.en: Judging art is an inherently subjective process.
sentences.az: İncəsənəti qiymətləndirmək mahiyyət etibarilə subyektiv prosesdir.

usage: INHERENT describes a quality that is a basic, permanent part of something and cannot be removed. It usually comes before a noun (an inherent weakness) or is followed by IN (dangers inherent in the system). Compare INTRINSIC (belonging to the essential nature of a thing; often of value) and INNATE (present from birth; of people and animals). INHERENTLY is common before adjectives: inherently dangerous, inherently unstable.

expressions.usage: flooding = large amounts of water covering an area that is usually dry
hazard = something that can be dangerous
fallout = the bad results of a situation
penalty = a punishment for breaking a law or rule
inflation = a general rise in prices
disruption = a situation in which something cannot continue normally
partially = not completely
Legal phrase: say something in mitigation

sentences.en: Planting trees can help to mitigate flooding.
sentences.az: Ağac əkmək daşqınların təsirini azaltmağa kömək edə bilər.

sentences.en: Governments must act now to mitigate the effects of climate change.
sentences.az: Hökumətlər iqlim dəyişikliyinin təsirlərini azaltmaq üçün indi hərəkətə keçməlidirlər.

sentences.en: The extra payments only partially mitigate the rise in prices.
sentences.az: Əlavə ödənişlər qiymət artımını yalnız qismən yumşaldır.

sentences.en: The party was an unmitigated disaster.
sentences.az: Qonaqlıq başdan-başa fəlakət oldu.

usage: MITIGATE means to make something less harmful, serious or painful. In climate science, MITIGATION (reducing emissions) is contrasted with ADAPTATION (adjusting to the changes). In law, MITIGATING CIRCUMSTANCES are facts that make a crime less serious. Do not confuse MITIGATE with MILITATE: "militate against" means to make something less likely. UNMITIGATED is used before negative nouns for emphasis: an unmitigated disaster.

expressions.usage: prevalent AMONG a group / IN a place
particularly = more than usual
misconception = a belief that is not correct
stereotype = a fixed idea about a type of person
ideology = a set of political beliefs
diabetes = a disease in which the body cannot control blood sugar
norm = a standard of behaviour that is typical of a group
justice = fair treatment according to the law

sentences.en: The disease is particularly prevalent among older people.
sentences.az: Bu xəstəlik xüsusilə yaşlı insanlar arasında geniş yayılıb.

sentences.en: It is a prevalent misconception that bats are blind.
sentences.az: Yarasaların kor olması geniş yayılmış yanlış təsəvvürdür.

sentences.en: The prevalence of diabetes has doubled in twenty years.
sentences.az: Şəkərli diabetin yayılma dərəcəsi iyirmi ildə iki dəfə artıb.

sentences.en: We believe that justice will prevail in the end.
sentences.az: İnanırıq ki, sonda ədalət qalib gələcək.

usage: PREVALENT means existing or happening very commonly at a particular time or in a particular place; it is typical of medical and sociological writing ("the prevalence of obesity"). PREVAILING describes what is most common or powerful now: the prevailing view, prevailing winds. The verb PREVAIL means to win after a struggle (prevail OVER an enemy) or to be accepted ("Common sense prevailed"). COMMON and WIDESPREAD are more general synonyms.

expressions.usage: influence = the power to affect how somebody thinks or behaves
implication = a possible future effect of an action
grief = great sadness, especially when somebody dies
gratitude = the feeling of being thankful
transformation = a complete change
admiration = a feeling of great respect and liking
deaf = unable to hear
sceptical = having doubts that something is true

sentences.en: Her grandmother had a profound influence on her life.
sentences.az: Nənəsi onun həyatına dərin təsir göstərib.

sentences.en: The discovery has profound implications for medicine.
sentences.az: Bu kəşfin tibb üçün ciddi nəticələri var.

sentences.en: I would like to express my profound gratitude to all my colleagues.
sentences.az: Bütün həmkarlarıma dərin minnətdarlığımı bildirmək istərdim.

sentences.en: The country has undergone a profound transformation in the last thirty years.
sentences.az: Ölkə son otuz ildə köklü dəyişiklik keçirib.

usage: PROFOUND is used with effects and feelings (a profound effect, profound sadness) and with ideas that show great knowledge (a profound book). DEEP is its everyday synonym, but PROFOUND is not used for physical depth: "deep water", not "profound water". PROFOUNDLY intensifies adjectives: profoundly affected, profoundly different, profoundly deaf. It is a strong, formal word; keep it for really important changes.

expressions.usage: be / come UNDER scrutiny
parliamentary = connected with a parliament
judicial = connected with judges and courts of law
escape = avoid something unpleasant
withstand = be strong enough not to be harmed by
heightened = made stronger or greater
international = involving several countries
expenditure = the amount of money spent

sentences.en: The company's finances have come under scrutiny.
sentences.az: Şirkətin maliyyə vəziyyəti ciddi nəzarət altına düşüb.

sentences.en: His argument does not withstand close scrutiny.
sentences.az: Onun dəlili diqqətli araşdırmaya tab gətirmir.

sentences.en: The new law was passed with very little parliamentary scrutiny.
sentences.az: Yeni qanun parlamentdə demək olar ki, müzakirə olunmadan qəbul edildi.

sentences.en: A committee was set up to scrutinise public expenditure.
sentences.az: Dövlət xərclərini diqqətlə yoxlamaq üçün komitə yaradıldı.

usage: SCRUTINY is careful and thorough examination, often critical. It is uncountable: "close scrutiny", "intense public scrutiny". The fixed pattern is "be / come UNDER scrutiny". Verbs: face, withstand, bear, escape, avoid scrutiny; subject something TO scrutiny. SCRUTINISE (American: scrutinize) is stronger than EXAMINE or CHECK and suggests looking for faults.

expressions.usage: authority = the power to give orders
trust = the belief that somebody is honest and reliable
credibility = the quality of being believed
morale = the confidence and enthusiasm of a group
foundation = the base on which something stands
self-esteem = a feeling of being happy with your own character and abilities
integrity = the state of being whole; also honesty
fatally = in a way that causes failure or death

sentences.en: The scandal has undermined public trust in the police.
sentences.az: Qalmaqal ictimaiyyətin polisə etimadını sarsıdıb.

sentences.en: Constant criticism can undermine a child's self-esteem.
sentences.az: Daimi tənqid uşağın özünə hörmətini sarsıda bilər.

sentences.en: Parents should not undermine a teacher's authority.
sentences.az: Valideynlər müəllimin nüfuzunu sarsıtmamalıdırlar.

sentences.en: The leak fatally undermined the minister's credibility.
sentences.az: Məlumat sızması nazirin etibarına sağalmaz zərbə vurdu.

usage: UNDERMINE means to make something weaker or less effective gradually, often secretly. Literally it means to dig under a wall so that it falls. Its objects are abstract: confidence, authority, position, credibility, efforts, democracy. Compare WEAKEN (general), ERODE (slowly destroy over time) and SABOTAGE (damage deliberately). It is a favourite verb in argumentative essays: "This would undermine the principle of equality."

lessons.azerbaijani: həyata keçirilə bilən, yaşamaq qabiliyyəti olan, səmərəli

expressions.usage: proposition = an offer or plan, especially in business
livelihood = the way you earn the money you need to live
substitute = a thing used in place of another
enterprise = a company or business
route = a way from one place to another
barely = only just; almost not
model = a system that can be copied by others
ensure = make certain that something happens

sentences.en: Solar power is now a viable alternative to coal.
sentences.az: Günəş enerjisi artıq kömürə real alternativdir.

sentences.en: Without more customers, the shop is barely viable.
sentences.az: Daha çox müştəri olmasa, mağaza güclə ayaqda durur.

sentences.en: Small farms are no longer a viable livelihood for many families.
sentences.az: Kiçik təsərrüfatlar artıq bir çox ailənin dolanışığını təmin etmir.

sentences.en: The loan will ensure the viability of the project.
sentences.az: Kredit layihənin yaşamaq qabiliyyətini təmin edəcək.

usage: VIABLE describes a plan, business or method that can work successfully. It often follows an adverb: commercially viable, economically viable, financially viable. Compare FEASIBLE (possible to do) – a project may be feasible but not viable if it cannot survive or make money. The most common nouns after it are ALTERNATIVE, OPTION, SOLUTION and BUSINESS. In biology, VIABLE means able to live: viable seeds.

expressions.usage: The preposition is ON (or ABOUT)
decide / govern by consensus
fragile = easily broken or destroyed
overwhelming = very great in amount
cross-party = involving several political parties
forge = create something strong with effort
tacit = understood without being said
in favour of = supporting

sentences.en: There is a growing consensus on the need for reform.
sentences.az: İslahatın zəruriliyi barədə getdikcə daha çox ümumi razılıq yaranır.

sentences.en: Decisions in the committee are taken by consensus.
sentences.az: Komitədə qərarlar ümumi razılıq əsasında qəbul edilir.

sentences.en: There is an overwhelming consensus among scientists that the climate is changing.
sentences.az: Alimlərin böyük əksəriyyəti iqlimin dəyişdiyi barədə yekdil rəydədir.

sentences.en: The prime minister tried to forge a consensus between the two sides.
sentences.az: Baş nazir iki tərəf arasında razılıq əldə etməyə çalışdı.

usage: CONSENSUS is general agreement among the members of a group. It is singular and usually takes "a" or "the": "reach a consensus", "the consensus is that ...". The spelling is conSENsus (it is not related to "census"). "Consensus of opinion" is common but is criticised as repetitive, because consensus already means agreement of opinion. Typical verbs: reach, achieve, build, forge a consensus; a consensus emerges or breaks down.

expressions.usage: Impersonal pattern + infinitive
timetable = a plan of when things will happen
render = cause something to be in a particular state (formal)
compromise = an agreement in which each side gives up something
entirely = completely
remedy = a way of dealing with a problem
explore = examine carefully to find out more
demonstrate = show clearly by giving proof

sentences.en: It is not feasible to finish the work by Friday.
sentences.az: İşi cümə gününə qədər bitirmək mümkün deyil.

sentences.en: New technology has rendered the project feasible.
sentences.az: Yeni texnologiya layihəni mümkün edib.

sentences.en: The council is exploring the feasibility of building a new bridge.
sentences.az: Bələdiyyə yeni körpü tikməyin mümkünlüyünü araşdırır.

sentences.en: We need a plan with a feasible timetable.
sentences.az: Bizə icrası mümkün qrafiki olan plan lazımdır.

usage: FEASIBLE means possible and practical to do, given the time, money and technology available. A FEASIBILITY STUDY examines whether a project is worth starting. Adverbs: technically feasible, economically feasible, perfectly feasible. Compare POSSIBLE (can happen), FEASIBLE (can be done in practice), VIABLE (can succeed and survive) and PLAUSIBLE (can be believed). The negative forms are "not feasible", UNFEASIBLE and INFEASIBLE.

lessons.azerbaijani: inkişafına kömək etmək, təşviq etmək; himayəyə götürmək

expressions.usage: creativity = the ability to produce new and original ideas
spirit = a particular attitude or feeling
goodwill = friendly feelings towards other people
curiosity = a strong desire to know about things
unity = the state of being joined together and in agreement
harmony = a state of peaceful agreement
resentment = a feeling of anger about something unfair

expressions.az: inklüzivliyi (hər kəsin cəlb olunmasını) təşviq etmək
expressions.usage: inclusion = making sure that everyone is able to take part

sentences.en: Good schools foster creativity as well as knowledge.
sentences.az: Yaxşı məktəblər biliklə yanaşı yaradıcılığı da inkişaf etdirir.

sentences.en: The club aims to foster a spirit of cooperation among young people.
sentences.az: Klub gənclər arasında əməkdaşlıq ruhunu aşılamağı qarşısına məqsəd qoyub.

sentences.en: Such unfair treatment only fosters resentment.
sentences.az: Belə ədalətsiz rəftar yalnız kin-küdurət yaradır.

sentences.en: They have fostered several children over the years.
sentences.az: Onlar bu illər ərzində bir neçə uşağı himayəyə götürüblər.

usage: FOSTER means to encourage something good to develop over time: foster understanding, foster relations, foster a sense of community. It can also be used of negative feelings (foster resentment). Its second meaning is to take another person's child into your home for a period without becoming the legal parent – compare ADOPT, which is permanent. As an adjective: foster parents, a foster child, foster care. Synonyms: PROMOTE, ENCOURAGE, NURTURE, CULTIVATE.

expressions.usage: investigation = an official examination of the facts
mobility = the ability to move easily
search = an attempt to find somebody or something
Pattern: hinder + object + FROM + -ing
productivity = the rate at which goods are produced
delivery = taking goods or services to people
visibility = how far you can see
Formal: move / travel without hindrance

sentences.en: Heavy snow hindered the search for the missing climbers.
sentences.az: Güclü qar itkin düşmüş alpinistlərin axtarışına mane oldu.

sentences.en: Lack of sleep can seriously hinder productivity.
sentences.az: Yuxusuzluq məhsuldarlığı ciddi şəkildə aşağı sala bilər.

sentences.en: Fog hindered visibility on the motorway.
sentences.az: Duman avtomagistralda görmə məsafəsini məhdudlaşdırdı.

sentences.en: High costs hinder many young people from starting a business.
sentences.az: Yüksək xərclər bir çox gəncin biznes qurmasına mane olur.

usage: HINDER means to make it difficult for something to happen or for somebody to do something; unlike PREVENT, it does not stop it completely. Patterns: hinder something; hinder somebody FROM doing something. The noun HINDRANCE loses the "e": hinder – hindrance. "More of a hindrance than a help" is a common phrase. Synonyms: HAMPER, IMPEDE (formal), OBSTRUCT (block deliberately). Opposites: HELP, FACILITATE.

expressions.usage: excuse = a reason that you give to explain bad behaviour
scenario = a description of how things might happen
hypothesis = an idea that has not yet been proved
interpretation = the particular way in which something is understood
seem = give the impression of being
pretext = a false reason given to hide the real one
superficially = only on the surface
coincidence = two things happening at the same time by chance

sentences.en: She could not think of a plausible excuse for being late.
sentences.az: O, gecikməsi üçün ağlabatan bəhanə fikirləşə bilmədi.

sentences.en: The explanation seems plausible, but there is no evidence for it.
sentences.az: İzah ağlabatan görünür, amma onu təsdiq edən sübut yoxdur.

sentences.en: Scientists have put forward several plausible hypotheses.
sentences.az: Alimlər bir neçə ağlabatan fərziyyə irəli sürüblər.

sentences.en: The plot of the film depends on a rather implausible coincidence.
sentences.az: Filmin süjeti olduqca inanılmaz bir təsadüf üzərində qurulub.

usage: PLAUSIBLE describes an explanation or statement that seems reasonable and likely to be true, although it has not been proved. It can also describe a person who is good at sounding honest when they may not be: "a plausible liar". Do not confuse PLAUSIBLE (believable) with POSSIBLE (can happen) or FEASIBLE (can be done). The opposite is IMPLAUSIBLE. A useful hedge for essays: "It is plausible that ...".

n.az: dayanıqlılıq, çətinlikdən sonra bərpa olunma qabiliyyəti

expressions.usage: remarkably = in a way that is unusual and surprising
setback = a problem that delays progress
adversity = a difficult or unpleasant situation
drought = a long period without rain
crop = a plant grown in large quantities for food
psychological = connected with the mind
enhance = improve the quality or strength of
inner = private and inside your mind

sentences.en: Children are often remarkably resilient.
sentences.az: Uşaqlar çox vaxt heyrətamiz dərəcədə dayanıqlı olurlar.

sentences.en: The economy has proved resilient to external shocks.
sentences.az: İqtisadiyyat xarici sarsıntılara qarşı dayanıqlı olduğunu göstərdi.

sentences.en: Farmers are being encouraged to plant climate-resilient crops.
sentences.az: Fermerlər iqlim dəyişikliyinə davamlı bitkilər əkməyə təşviq olunurlar.

sentences.en: Sport can enhance young people's psychological resilience.
sentences.az: İdman gənclərin psixoloji dayanıqlılığını artıra bilər.

usage: RESILIENT describes people, economies and systems that can recover quickly after difficulties. RESILIENCE has become a key word in psychology, economics and climate policy. Patterns: resilient TO shocks; resilience IN THE FACE OF difficulties. Compare TOUGH (strong enough to deal with hard conditions), ROBUST (strong and unlikely to fail) and DURABLE (lasting a long time; of products). Of materials, resilient means returning to the original shape after being bent.

expressions.usage: selection = the process of choosing
enforcement = making sure that a law is obeyed
inspection = an official visit to check that rules are being obeyed
evaluation = a careful judgement about how good something is
methodology = the set of methods used in a study
intellectually = in a way connected with thinking and reasoning
monitor = watch and check over a period of time
Plural noun: the rigours of winter / of army life

sentences.en: All new drugs undergo rigorous testing before they are sold.
sentences.az: Bütün yeni dərmanlar satışa çıxarılmazdan əvvəl ciddi sınaqdan keçir.

sentences.en: The study was praised for its rigorous methodology.
sentences.az: Tədqiqat dəqiq metodologiyasına görə təriflənib.

sentences.en: Air quality in the city is rigorously monitored.
sentences.az: Şəhərdə havanın keyfiyyəti ciddi nəzarətdə saxlanılır.

sentences.en: Few plants can survive the rigours of a mountain winter.
sentences.az: Dağ qışının sərtliyinə az bitki tab gətirə bilir.

usage: RIGOROUS describes work that is careful, thorough and exact (rigorous analysis, rigorous testing) or rules that are strictly applied (rigorous standards). British English spells the noun RIGOUR but the adjective RIGOROUS, without the second "u"; American English writes "rigor". Compare THOROUGH (complete, with attention to detail) and STRICT (demanding that rules are obeyed). "Academic rigour" is a quality expected of university work.

expressions.usage: divorce = the legal ending of a marriage
associated with = connected with
addiction = being unable to stop taking or doing something harmful
disability = a physical or mental condition that limits activity
combat = try to stop something harmful
shame = the painful feeling of having done something wrong
prejudice = an unfair dislike of a group of people
Passive pattern + AS

sentences.en: There is still a stigma associated with mental illness.
sentences.az: Psixi xəstəliklə bağlı damğa hələ də qalmaqdadır.

sentences.en: The campaign aims to combat stigma and prejudice.
sentences.az: Kampaniyanın məqsədi damğalanma və qərəzli münasibətlə mübarizə aparmaqdır.

sentences.en: In the past, the stigma of divorce was much greater.
sentences.az: Keçmişdə boşanmanın ictimai qınağı daha güclü idi.

sentences.en: Children from poor families should not be stigmatised as failures.
sentences.az: Yoxsul ailələrdən olan uşaqlar uğursuz kimi damğalanmamalıdırlar.

usage: STIGMA is the negative feeling that society has about a particular condition or behaviour, such as mental illness, unemployment or poverty. It is usually uncountable or singular: "a stigma attached to ...", "the stigma of ...". Typical verbs: carry a stigma, remove / reduce / overcome the stigma. STIGMATISE (American: stigmatize) is mostly passive. The word is valuable for IELTS topics on health and social issues.

expressions.usage: disparity BETWEEN two groups; disparity IN income
glaring = very easily seen; said of something bad
regional = connected with a particular part of a country
gender = the fact of being male or female
wage = money paid for work, usually weekly or by the hour
persist = continue to exist
narrow = make smaller
stark = very obvious and unpleasant

sentences.en: There is a glaring disparity between the rich and the poor in the city.
sentences.az: Şəhərdə varlılarla yoxsullar arasında göz qabağında olan kəskin fərq var.

sentences.en: The government wants to reduce regional disparities in income.
sentences.az: Hökumət gəlirlərdə regionlar arasındakı fərqləri azaltmaq istəyir.

sentences.en: Wage disparity between men and women has narrowed, but it has not disappeared.
sentences.az: Kişilərlə qadınlar arasında əməkhaqqı fərqi azalıb, amma aradan qalxmayıb.

sentences.en: Despite the reforms, serious disparities persist.
sentences.az: İslahatlara baxmayaraq, ciddi fərqlər qalmaqda davam edir.

usage: A DISPARITY is a difference, especially one that is unfair: a disparity BETWEEN groups, a disparity IN pay, health or opportunity. It is stronger and more formal than DIFFERENCE and close to INEQUALITY and GAP. Useful collocations for IELTS Task 2: "the growing disparity between rich and poor", "address regional disparities". Do not confuse it with DISCREPANCY, a difference between two things that should be the same (figures, accounts, statements).

expressions.usage: The preposition is TO
welfare = the general health, happiness and safety of people
biodiversity = the variety of plants and animals in an area
ecosystem = all the living things in an area and their environment
mutually = felt or done equally by both sides
concentration = the ability to give all your attention to one thing
Formal fixed phrase
Formal fixed phrase

sentences.en: Too much screen time can be detrimental to children's health.
sentences.az: Ekran qarşısında həddindən artıq vaxt keçirmək uşaqların sağlamlığına zərərli ola bilər.

sentences.en: The use of pesticides is detrimental to biodiversity.
sentences.az: Pestisidlərdən istifadə biomüxtəlifliyə zərərlidir.

sentences.en: He worked long hours, to the detriment of his family life.
sentences.az: O, ailə həyatının zərərinə uzun saatlar işləyirdi.

sentences.en: Constant noise is detrimental to concentration.
sentences.az: Daimi səs-küy diqqətin cəmlənməsinə mane olur.

usage: DETRIMENTAL is a formal synonym of HARMFUL and DAMAGING. It is almost always followed by TO: "detrimental to health", or used before EFFECT or IMPACT: "a detrimental effect on the environment". The noun appears mainly in two fixed phrases: "to the detriment of" (resulting in harm to) and "without detriment to". The opposite is BENEFICIAL. It is an excellent upgrade for "bad for" in formal essays.

expressions.usage: reserve = a supply kept for future use
ozone = a gas high above the Earth; layer = a thin sheet of a substance
battery = a device that stores electricity
nutrient = a substance that plants and animals need to grow
groundwater = water found under the ground
oxygen = the gas in the air that we need to breathe
squad = a group of players from which a team is chosen
oil = the thick liquid from under the ground used for fuel

sentences.en: Overfishing has seriously depleted fish stocks in the North Sea.
sentences.az: Həddindən artıq balıq ovu Şimal dənizində balıq ehtiyatlarını ciddi şəkildə azaldıb.

sentences.en: Certain chemicals deplete the ozone layer.
sentences.az: Bəzi kimyəvi maddələr ozon təbəqəsini dağıdır.

sentences.en: Growing the same crop every year depletes nutrients in the soil.
sentences.az: Hər il eyni bitkini əkmək torpaqdakı qida maddələrini tükədir.

sentences.en: Using the camera a lot will quickly deplete the battery.
sentences.az: Kameradan çox istifadə etmək batareyanı tez boşaldacaq.

usage: DEPLETE means to reduce the amount of something so that there is not enough left; it is usually passive: "Stocks are seriously depleted." It is typical of environmental writing: deplete natural resources, the depletion of the ozone layer. Compare EXHAUST (use up completely), DRAIN (use up strength, money or energy) and RUN OUT OF (informal). The opposite is REPLENISH (fill again).

lessons.azerbaijani: bəyənmək, dəstəkləmək, təsdiq etmək; (məhsulu) reklam etmək

n.az: dəstək, təsdiq, həmçinin reklam xarakterli tövsiyə

expressions.usage: officially = publicly and by somebody in authority
treaty = a formal agreement between countries
motion = a formal proposal discussed and voted on at a meeting
verdict = a decision made by a jury, or an official judgement
wholeheartedly = completely and with enthusiasm
unanimously = with the agreement of everyone
celebrity = a famous person
ringing = here: strong and clear

sentences.en: The committee unanimously endorsed the proposal.
sentences.az: Komitə təklifi yekdilliklə dəstəklədi.

sentences.en: I wholeheartedly endorse everything she has said.
sentences.az: Onun dediyi hər şeyi ürəkdən dəstəkləyirəm.

sentences.en: The party has officially endorsed her as its candidate.
sentences.az: Partiya onu rəsmən öz namizədi kimi dəstəkləyib.

sentences.en: Celebrity endorsements can increase sales dramatically.
sentences.az: Məşhurların dəstəyi satışları kəskin artıra bilər.

usage: ENDORSE means to say publicly that you support a person, statement or course of action. In advertising it means that a famous person says they use and like a product. In British English a driving licence can also be "endorsed" with a record of an offence. Compare APPROVE (officially accept), BACK (support, less formal) and RATIFY (make a treaty officially valid). The noun takes OF or FROM: "an endorsement of the plan".

expressions.usage: cliff = a high area of rock with a very steep side, often by the sea
faith = trust in somebody or something
boundary = a line that marks a limit
sovereignty = a country's power to govern itself
privacy = the state of being free from public attention
civil = connected with citizens; liberty = freedom
soil = the top layer of the earth in which plants grow
coastal = of the land beside the sea

sentences.en: The sea is slowly eroding the cliffs.
sentences.az: Dəniz qayalıqları yavaş-yavaş aşındırır.

sentences.en: Repeated scandals have eroded public faith in politicians.
sentences.az: Təkrarlanan qalmaqallar ictimaiyyətin siyasətçilərə inamını zəiflədib.

sentences.en: Cutting down forests leads to soil erosion.
sentences.az: Meşələrin qırılması torpaq eroziyasına gətirib çıxarır.

sentences.en: Critics say the new law will erode civil liberties.
sentences.az: Tənqidçilər yeni qanunun vətəndaş azadlıqlarını məhdudlaşdıracağını deyirlər.

usage: ERODE literally describes the gradual destruction of rock or soil by sea, wind or rain. Figuratively it means to destroy something gradually: erode confidence, erode support, erode the value of savings. It is both transitive and intransitive ("Support has eroded"). Compare UNDERMINE (weaken, often deliberately) and CORRODE (destroy metal by chemical action). The noun EROSION is uncountable.

expressions.usage: militarily = by using soldiers and weapons
dispute = a serious argument or disagreement
promptly = without delay
reluctant = not willing to do something
force = make somebody do something they do not want to do
humanitarian = concerned with reducing suffering
divine = coming from God
surgical = connected with medical operations

sentences.en: The police had to intervene to stop the fight.
sentences.az: Polis davanı dayandırmaq üçün müdaxilə etməli oldu.

sentences.en: The central bank was forced to intervene to support the currency.
sentences.az: Mərkəzi bank valyutanı dəstəkləmək üçün müdaxilə etməyə məcbur oldu.

sentences.en: The government was reluctant to intervene in the dispute.
sentences.az: Hökumət mübahisəyə müdaxilə etməyə meyilli deyildi.

sentences.en: In severe cases, surgical intervention may be necessary.
sentences.az: Ağır hallarda cərrahi müdaxilə lazım ola bilər.

usage: INTERVENE means to become involved in a situation in order to improve it or stop it getting worse. It is intransitive and takes IN: "intervene IN a conflict". INTERFERE has a negative meaning – to get involved where you are not wanted. "State intervention" is government action in the economy. INTERVENING before a noun means "between two events": "in the intervening years". "Early intervention" is a key term in education and health care.

expressions.usage: expectation = a belief that something will happen
grievance = something that you think is unfair and complain about
criticism = the act of saying what is wrong with something
objection = a reason why you do not agree with something
transaction = a piece of business, such as buying or selling
protest = a public expression of strong disagreement
confer = give an official right or quality (formal)
regime = a government, especially one that was not fairly elected

sentences.en: The workers have a legitimate grievance about their pay.
sentences.az: İşçilərin əməkhaqları ilə bağlı əsaslı narazılığı var.

sentences.en: That is a perfectly legitimate question.
sentences.az: Bu, tamamilə əsaslı sualdır.

sentences.en: Free elections confer legitimacy on a government.
sentences.az: Azad seçkilər hökumətə legitimlik verir.

sentences.en: Peaceful protest is a legitimate part of democratic life.
sentences.az: Dinc etiraz demokratik həyatın qanuni tərkib hissəsidir.

usage: LEGITIMATE means allowed by law (a legitimate business) or fair and reasonable (a legitimate concern, a legitimate question). LEGAL simply means "not against the law"; LEGITIMATE adds the idea of being right or justified. The adjective ends in a weak syllable, /lɪˈdʒɪtɪmət/. LEGITIMACY is a central term in politics: the right of a government to rule. The opposite is ILLEGITIMATE.

expressions.usage: hint = something that you say in an indirect way
flavour = the particular taste of a food or drink
humour = the quality of being funny
shade = a particular type of a colour
irony = saying the opposite of what you mean, often as a joke
clue = a fact that helps to solve a mystery
blend = a mixture of different types of the same thing
alter = change slightly

sentences.en: There is a subtle difference between the two words.
sentences.az: Bu iki söz arasında incə bir fərq var.

sentences.en: She dropped a subtle hint that she wanted to leave.
sentences.az: O, getmək istədiyinə incə bir işarə vurdu.

sentences.en: The sauce has a subtle flavour of lemon.
sentences.az: Sousun zərif limon dadı var.

sentences.en: The author's subtle irony is easy to miss.
sentences.az: Müəllifin incə istehzasını sezməmək asandır.

usage: The "b" in SUBTLE is silent: /ˈsʌtəl/, and so it is in SUBTLETY and SUBTLY. SUBTLE describes something that is not obvious and is therefore difficult to notice or describe: subtle differences, subtle changes, subtle colours. It also describes people or methods that are clever and indirect. The spelling of the adverb is SUBTLY (not "subtlely"). The opposite ideas are OBVIOUS, CRUDE and BLATANT.

expressions.usage: chain = a series of connected things; reaction = a response to something
war = armed fighting between countries
explosion = the sudden, violent bursting of something such as a bomb
allergy = a condition that makes you ill when you eat or touch a particular thing
panic = a sudden feeling of great fear
backlash = a strong negative reaction by many people
outbreak = the sudden start of something unpleasant
pull = move something towards yourself; here "trigger" is a noun

sentences.en: The announcement triggered panic on the stock market.
sentences.az: Bu elan fond bazarında çaxnaşma yaratdı.

sentences.en: Certain foods can trigger an allergy.
sentences.az: Bəzi qidalar allergiya törədə bilər.

sentences.en: The decision triggered a backlash from parents.
sentences.az: Qərar valideynlərin kəskin əks-reaksiyasına səbəb oldu.

sentences.en: The collapse of one bank triggered a chain reaction.
sentences.az: Bir bankın iflası zəncirvari reaksiyaya səbəb oldu.

usage: As a verb, TRIGGER means to make something happen suddenly: trigger a reaction, a crisis, an alarm, a memory. It suggests that one small event starts a larger process, so it is more precise than CAUSE. As a noun, a trigger is the part of a gun that you pull, and also anything that starts a reaction: "Stress is a common trigger for headaches." Phrasal form: TRIGGER OFF. Synonyms: SPARK, PROMPT, SET OFF, PROVOKE.

expressions.usage: scale = the size or extent of something
prosperity = the state of being successful and rich
surge = a sudden large increase
era = a period of history
expansion = an increase in size or number
turmoil = a state of great confusion and uncertainty
virtually = almost
Formal fixed phrase

sentences.en: The floods caused damage on an unprecedented scale.
sentences.az: Daşqınlar misli görünməmiş miqyasda ziyan vurdu.

sentences.en: The country is enjoying a period of unprecedented prosperity.
sentences.az: Ölkə misli görünməmiş rifah dövrünü yaşayır.

sentences.en: There has been an unprecedented surge in demand for online courses.
sentences.az: Onlayn kurslara tələbatda misli görünməmiş kəskin artım olub.

sentences.en: Such a decision is without precedent in the history of the court.
sentences.az: Belə bir qərarın məhkəmənin tarixində presedenti yoxdur.

usage: UNPRECEDENTED means never having happened or existed before. It is much stronger than "unusual", so use it only for truly exceptional events. A PRECEDENT is an earlier event or legal decision that serves as an example for later ones: "set a precedent", "a legal precedent". The stress falls on the second syllable of the adjective (unPREcedented) and on the first syllable of the noun (PREcedent).

expressions.usage: infection = a disease caused by bacteria or a virus
abuse = cruel or unfair treatment
fraud = the crime of deceiving people to get money

expressions.az: nəsli kəsilmək təhlükəsi ilə üz-üzə olan
expressions.usage: extinction = the situation in which a species no longer exists
habitat = the natural home of a plant or animal
elderly = old (a polite word for people)
household = all the people living together in one home
expose = show something that is usually hidden

sentences.en: Young children are particularly vulnerable to infection.
sentences.az: Kiçik uşaqlar infeksiyaya qarşı xüsusilə həssasdırlar.

sentences.en: The scheme provides free meals for the elderly and vulnerable.
sentences.az: Layihə yaşlılara və müdafiəsiz təbəqələrə pulsuz yemək verir.

sentences.en: Many species are vulnerable to extinction because of habitat loss.
sentences.az: Yaşayış mühitinin itirilməsi səbəbindən bir çox növ nəslinin kəsilməsi təhlükəsi ilə üz-üzədir.

sentences.en: The attack exposed a serious vulnerability in the bank's software.
sentences.az: Hücum bankın proqram təminatındakı ciddi zəif nöqtəni üzə çıxardı.

usage: VULNERABLE means able to be easily hurt, harmed or attacked, physically or emotionally. It takes TO: "vulnerable TO attack / criticism / disease". "The vulnerable" and "vulnerable groups" are standard terms in social policy for people who need special care or protection. VULNERABILITY is uncountable for the general state and countable for a specific weak point, especially in computing. The first "l" is pronounced: /ˈvʌlnərəbəl/.

lessons.azerbaijani: pay, maraq; risk altında olan məbləğ; paya, dirək

expressions.usage: Fixed phrase: be at stake = could be won or lost
stake IN a company / IN the future
majority = more than half of the total
acquire = get or buy (formal)

expressions.az: ərazini öz nəzarətinə götürmək, sərhədini müəyyən etmək
expressions.usage: territory = an area that one person or group controls; phrasal verb
consult = ask for advice or opinions
involve = make somebody take part in something
relevant = closely connected with the subject

sentences.en: Thousands of jobs are at stake.
sentences.az: Minlərlə iş yeri risk altındadır.

sentences.en: The company has acquired a majority stake in its main rival.
sentences.az: Şirkət əsas rəqibinin nəzarət payını əldə edib.

sentences.en: Young people have a stake in the future of the planet.
sentences.az: Planetin gələcəyində gənclərin payı var.

sentences.en: The council promised to consult all relevant stakeholders before making a decision.
sentences.az: Bələdiyyə qərar verməzdən əvvəl bütün müvafiq maraqlı tərəflərlə məsləhətləşməyə söz verdi.

usage: AT STAKE means that something valuable may be lost if a situation develops badly: "Our reputation is at stake." A STAKE in a business is a share of it; "have a stake in something" means its success matters to you. The STAKES are the things that can be gained or lost: "The stakes are high." A STAKEHOLDER is any person or group affected by a project or organisation – a key term in business and policy writing. As a verb: "stake your reputation ON something".

lessons.azerbaijani: dözmək, tab gətirmək; daşımaq, öz üzərində saxlamaq; (uşaq) doğmaq

expressions.usage: resemblance = the fact of looking like somebody or something

expressions.az: ən ağır zərbəni öz üzərinə götürmək
expressions.usage: brunt = the main force of something unpleasant; used only in this phrase

expressions.az: nəyəsə şahidlik etmək, nəyisə sübut etmək
expressions.usage: witness = a person who sees an event
grudge = a feeling of anger towards somebody because of the past
scar = a mark left on the skin by a wound
hallmark = a typical feature
grin = smile widely; idiom
agony = extreme physical or mental pain

sentences.en: She bears a striking resemblance to her mother.
sentences.az: O, anasına heyrətamiz dərəcədə bənzəyir.

sentences.en: Small businesses will bear the brunt of the tax rises.
sentences.az: Vergi artımının ən ağır zərbəsi kiçik müəssisələrə dəyəcək.

sentences.en: He is not the kind of person who bears a grudge.
sentences.az: O, kin saxlayan adam deyil.

sentences.en: I can't bear the thought of losing her.
sentences.az: Onu itirmək fikrinə dözə bilmirəm.

usage: BEAR is irregular: bear – bore – borne. Its core meanings are to carry (bear a name, bear the cost, bear responsibility) and to accept something unpleasant ("I can't bear the noise"), where it is close to STAND and TOLERATE. Key phrases: BEAR IN MIND (remember to consider), BEAR WITH ME (please be patient), BEAR OUT (confirm: "The figures bear out his claim"). The passive "be born" is spelt without "e". The noun BEAR is the animal – a different word.

lessons.unit: Academic verbs for processes and ideas

expressions.usage: dust = dry dirt in the form of powder
savings = money that you have saved
possession = something that you own
fat = the substance under the skin that stores energy
toxin = a poisonous substance
asset = something valuable that a person or company owns
total = the number you get by adding everything together
surplus = an amount that is more than is needed

sentences.en: Dust had accumulated on the shelves.
sentences.az: Rəflərin üstünə toz yığılmışdı.

sentences.en: Over the years she accumulated enough savings to buy a flat.
sentences.az: İllər ərzində o, mənzil almaq üçün kifayət qədər yığım topladı.

sentences.en: Toxins can accumulate in the body over time.
sentences.az: Toksinlər zaman keçdikcə orqanizmdə toplana bilər.

sentences.en: The cumulative total for the year was three million pounds.
sentences.az: İl üzrə məcmu yekun üç milyon funt təşkil etdi.

usage: ACCUMULATE means to collect or increase gradually over a period of time. It is transitive ("accumulate wealth") and intransitive ("Debts accumulated"). Compare COLLECT (bring together deliberately), GATHER (bring together from different places) and AMASS (collect a very large amount, especially money). CUMULATIVE describes an effect that grows with each addition: "the cumulative effect of small changes".

lessons.unit: Academic verbs for processes and ideas

expressions.usage: aspire TO + noun / infinitive
leadership = the position of being the leader
actor = a person who performs in plays or films
entrepreneur = a person who starts a business
fulfil = achieve something hoped for
lofty = noble and deserving admiration
thwart = prevent somebody from doing what they want
harbour = keep a feeling in your mind for a long time

sentences.en: She aspires to become a judge.
sentences.az: O, hakim olmağa can atır.

sentences.en: The course is designed for aspiring entrepreneurs.
sentences.az: Kurs sahibkar olmağa can atanlar üçün nəzərdə tutulub.

sentences.en: He never fulfilled his aspiration to study abroad.
sentences.az: O, xaricdə təhsil almaq arzusunu heç vaxt həyata keçirə bilmədi.

sentences.en: Poverty thwarted the aspirations of a whole generation.
sentences.az: Yoxsulluq bütöv bir nəslin arzularını puça çıxardı.

usage: ASPIRE means to have a strong desire to achieve something important. It takes TO: "aspire to a career in medicine", "aspire to be a doctor". ASPIRATIONS (usually plural) are strong hopes for the future: career aspirations, political aspirations. ASPIRING before a job title means "hoping to become": an aspiring writer. Compare AMBITION (a strong wish to be successful) and DREAM (less formal).

lessons.unit: Academic verbs for processes and ideas

expressions.usage: autonomy OVER decisions / budgets
individual = of one person rather than a group
region = a large area of a country
republic = a country with a president and no king or queen
editorial = connected with preparing a newspaper or book
function = work or operate
robot = a machine that can do tasks automatically
curtail = limit or reduce

sentences.en: Nakhchivan is an autonomous republic within Azerbaijan.
sentences.az: Naxçıvan Azərbaycanın tərkibində muxtar respublikadır.

sentences.en: Teachers should have more autonomy over what they teach.
sentences.az: Müəllimlərin nə tədris etdikləri üzərində daha çox sərbəstliyi olmalıdır.

sentences.en: Each department functions autonomously.
sentences.az: Hər şöbə müstəqil fəaliyyət göstərir.

sentences.en: The new law curtails the autonomy of universities.
sentences.az: Yeni qanun universitetlərin müstəqilliyini məhdudlaşdırır.

usage: AUTONOMY is the freedom of a country, region or organisation to govern itself, and also the ability of a person to act without being controlled by others. It is uncountable. Patterns: autonomy FROM a central government; autonomy OVER something. AUTONOMOUS describes self-governing regions and, in technology, machines that operate without human control: autonomous vehicles. Compare INDEPENDENCE (complete freedom from control) and SOVEREIGNTY (the full power of a state).

lessons.unit: Academic verbs for processes and ideas

expressions.usage: The preposition is FOR
serve = perform a function
chemical = connected with chemistry
revolution = an attempt to change a government by force; also a great change
regeneration = making an area active and successful again
unrest = angry or violent behaviour by people who are protesting
potent = having a strong effect
converter = a device that changes something into a different form

sentences.en: The scandal was a catalyst for change.
sentences.az: Qalmaqal dəyişiklik üçün katalizator oldu.

sentences.en: The new stadium served as a catalyst for the regeneration of the area.
sentences.az: Yeni stadion ərazinin dirçəlişi üçün katalizator rolunu oynadı.

sentences.en: Rising food prices were a catalyst for unrest.
sentences.az: Ərzaq qiymətlərinin artması iğtişaşlara təkan verən amil oldu.

sentences.en: A chemical catalyst speeds up a reaction without being used up.
sentences.az: Kimyəvi katalizator özü sərf olunmadan reaksiyanı sürətləndirir.

usage: In chemistry, a CATALYST is a substance that makes a reaction happen faster without being changed itself. Figuratively it is a person or event that causes an important change: "a catalyst FOR change" is the classic collocation. Typical verbs: act as, serve as, prove (to be) a catalyst. Compare TRIGGER (the immediate cause) and IMPETUS (a force that makes something happen more quickly). The British spelling of the verb is CATALYSE.

lessons.unit: Academic verbs for processes and ideas

expressions.usage: review = a careful examination of a situation
overview = a general description of a subject
database = an organised set of data stored in a computer
audit = an official examination of accounts or quality
handbook = a book giving instructions or information
overhaul = a thorough examination and improvement of a system
defeat = failure to win
beat = defeat somebody in a game or fight

sentences.en: The report gives a comprehensive overview of the housing market.
sentences.az: Hesabat mənzil bazarının əhatəli ümumi mənzərəsini verir.

sentences.en: The tax system needs a comprehensive overhaul.
sentences.az: Vergi sisteminin köklü yenidənqurmaya ehtiyacı var.

sentences.en: The government has ordered a comprehensive review of the policy.
sentences.az: Hökumət bu siyasətin hərtərəfli təhlilini tapşırıb.

sentences.en: Our team was comprehensively beaten in the final.
sentences.az: Komandamız finalda tamamilə məğlub oldu.

usage: COMPREHENSIVE means including all, or almost all, the details or facts: a comprehensive guide, comprehensive insurance (covering every kind of risk). In Britain a COMPREHENSIVE (school) is a state secondary school for pupils of all abilities. Do not confuse it with COMPREHENSIBLE (able to be understood); both come from COMPREHEND. Synonyms: THOROUGH, EXHAUSTIVE, EXTENSIVE, COMPLETE.

lessons.unit: Academic verbs for processes and ideas
lessons.azerbaijani: götür-qoy etmək, barəsində düşünmək; seyr etmək

expressions.usage: retirement = the time when you stop working because of your age
resignation = the act of giving up your job
emigration = leaving your own country to live in another
horizon = the line where the sky seems to meet the land or sea
awful = very bad or unpleasant
takeover = the act of taking control of a company
sabbatical = a long period of leave for study or travel
abyss = a very deep hole; a hopeless situation

sentences.en: At sixty he began to contemplate retirement.
sentences.az: Altmış yaşında o, təqaüdə çıxmaq barədə düşünməyə başladı.

sentences.en: The consequences of failure are too awful to contemplate.
sentences.az: Uğursuzluğun nəticələri barədə düşünmək belə dəhşətlidir.

sentences.en: She sat on the beach, contemplating the horizon.
sentences.az: O, çimərlikdə oturub üfüqü seyr edirdi.

sentences.en: The company is contemplating a takeover of its main rival.
sentences.az: Şirkət əsas rəqibini ələ keçirmək barədə düşünür.

usage: CONTEMPLATE means to think carefully about a possible future action, or to look at something thoughtfully for a long time. It is followed by a noun or -ing form: "contemplate leaving" – not "contemplate to leave". It is more formal and more serious than CONSIDER. CONTEMPLATION is deep thought, often religious or philosophical. Compare PONDER (think about carefully) and MULL OVER (informal).

lessons.unit: Academic verbs for processes and ideas

expressions.usage: correlate WITH something
correlation BETWEEN two variables
causation = the process of one event causing another
inverse = opposite in amount: when one rises, the other falls
coefficient = a number that measures a property
robust = strong and unlikely to fail
detect = discover or notice something that is not easy to see
modest = not very large

sentences.en: Poverty correlates strongly with poor health.
sentences.az: Yoxsulluq zəif sağlamlıqla sıx əlaqəlidir.

sentences.en: There is a clear correlation between education and income.
sentences.az: Təhsillə gəlir arasında aydın korrelyasiya var.

sentences.en: Researchers found an inverse correlation between exercise and stress.
sentences.az: Tədqiqatçılar idmanla stress arasında tərs korrelyasiya aşkar ediblər.

sentences.en: Students must learn the difference between correlation and causation.
sentences.az: Tələbələr korrelyasiya ilə səbəb-nəticə əlaqəsinin fərqini öyrənməlidirlər.

usage: To CORRELATE is to have a relationship in which one thing changes when the other does. The noun CORRELATION is central to statistics and to describing data: a strong / weak / positive / negative correlation BETWEEN A and B. The warning "correlation does not imply causation" means that two things happening together does not prove that one causes the other – a valuable point for critical essays.

lessons.unit: Academic verbs for processes and ideas
lessons.azerbaijani: (nə iləsə) yekunlaşmaq, ən yüksək nöqtəyə çatmaq

expressions.usage: culminate IN / WITH something
Noun pattern
riot = violent behaviour by a crowd in a public place
ceremony = a formal public or religious event
collapse = a sudden failure of a system or organisation
showdown = a final argument or fight that settles a dispute
arrest = the act of taking somebody to a police station
breakthrough = an important discovery or development

sentences.en: Months of protests culminated in a riot.
sentences.az: Aylarla davam edən etirazlar iğtişaşla nəticələndi.

sentences.en: The festival culminates in a ceremony on the main square.
sentences.az: Festival əsas meydanda keçirilən mərasimlə yekunlaşır.

sentences.en: The award was the culmination of forty years of work.
sentences.az: Bu mükafat qırx illik əməyin zirvəsi idi.

sentences.en: Years of research culminated in a breakthrough.
sentences.az: İllərlə aparılan tədqiqatlar mühüm irəliləyişlə nəticələndi.

usage: CULMINATE means to end with a particular result or to reach the highest point after a long development. It is intransitive and takes IN or WITH: "culminate IN victory". The subject is usually a process or series of events: talks, protests, a career, a campaign. Compare RESULT IN (neutral), END IN and CLIMAX. THE CULMINATION OF something is its final and most important point.

lessons.unit: Academic verbs for processes and ideas

expressions.usage: outline = the line that shows the shape of something
palate = the ability to recognise and enjoy good food and drink
audience = the people watching a play, film or concert
silhouette = the dark shape of something seen against light
mist = a thin cloud of very small drops of water in the air
trace = a very small amount; a sign that something was present
readily = quickly and easily
collector = a person who collects things as a hobby

sentences.en: I could just discern the silhouette of a ship through the mist.
sentences.az: Duman arasından güclə bir gəminin siluetini seçə bilirdim.

sentences.en: There has been no discernible improvement.
sentences.az: Heç bir sezilən yaxşılaşma olmayıb.

sentences.en: I discerned a trace of irony in her voice.
sentences.az: Onun səsində istehza izi sezdim.

sentences.en: The restaurant is popular with diners who have a discerning palate.
sentences.az: Restoran incə dad duyumu olan müştərilər arasında məşhurdur.

usage: DISCERN is a formal verb meaning to see or understand something that is not obvious: discern a pattern, discern a difference. It is not used in the progressive. DISCERNIBLE means able to be noticed ("no discernible difference"); DISCERNING is a word of praise for people with good judgement and taste ("a discerning reader"). Compare DETECT (discover something hidden), PERCEIVE (become aware of) and MAKE OUT (informal).

lessons.unit: Academic verbs for processes and ideas

expressions.usage: sympathy = the feeling of being sorry for somebody
confession = a statement admitting that you are guilty
laughter = the sound or act of laughing
applause = the noise of people clapping their hands
gasp = a quick deep breath caused by surprise
outrage = a strong feeling of shock and anger
compassion = a strong feeling of sympathy for people who are suffering
donation = money given to help a person or organisation

sentences.en: The police failed to elicit a confession.
sentences.az: Polis etiraf ala bilmədi.

sentences.en: His joke elicited laughter from the audience.
sentences.az: Onun zarafatı tamaşaçıların gülüşünə səbəb oldu.

sentences.en: The decision elicited outrage among parents.
sentences.az: Qərar valideynlər arasında qəzəb doğurdu.

sentences.en: The teacher tried to elicit the answer from the class.
sentences.az: Müəllim cavabı sinifdən almağa çalışdı.

usage: ELICIT means to get information or a reaction from somebody, often with difficulty: elicit a response, a reply, information, support. In language teaching, to elicit is to draw answers out of students instead of telling them. Do not confuse ELICIT /ɪˈlɪsɪt/ (verb) with ILLICIT (adjective: illegal) – they sound the same. Pattern: elicit something FROM somebody. Synonyms: DRAW OUT, EVOKE, OBTAIN.

expressions.usage: spectrum = a complete range of opinions or types
multitude = an extremely large number
array = a large and impressive group of things
continent = one of the large land masses of the Earth
suburb = an area where people live outside the centre of a city
century = a period of 100 years
genre = a particular type of art, film, music or literature
realm = an area of activity, interest or knowledge

sentences.en: The course encompasses a wide spectrum of subjects.
sentences.az: Kurs geniş fənn spektrini əhatə edir.

sentences.en: Her work encompasses many genres, from poetry to film.
sentences.az: Onun yaradıcılığı poeziyadan kinoya qədər bir çox janrı əhatə edir.

sentences.en: The new district encompasses the suburbs to the north of the city.
sentences.az: Yeni rayon şəhərin şimalındakı şəhərətrafı əraziləri əhatə edir.

sentences.en: The exhibition encompasses five centuries of Azerbaijani art.
sentences.az: Sərgi Azərbaycan incəsənətinin beş əsrini əhatə edir.

usage: ENCOMPASS means to include a large number or range of things, or to surround an area completely. It is formal; the subject is usually a study, plan, term or area. Compare INCLUDE (have as one part), COVER (deal with a subject), COMPRISE (consist of) and EMBRACE (include willingly). ALL-ENCOMPASSING means including everything: "an all-encompassing theory".

expressions.usage: consent = permission to do something
reference = a mention of something
sexually = in a way connected with sex
content = the material contained in a film, book or website
approval = official agreement
mention = refer to something briefly
prohibit = forbid by law or rule
The preposition is IN

sentences.en: Data may not be shared without the user's explicit consent.
sentences.az: İstifadəçinin açıq razılığı olmadan məlumatlar paylaşıla bilməz.

sentences.en: The contract explicitly prohibits working for a rival company.
sentences.az: Müqavilə rəqib şirkətdə işləməyi açıq şəkildə qadağan edir.

sentences.en: The report makes no explicit reference to the minister.
sentences.az: Hesabatda nazirə birbaşa istinad yoxdur.

sentences.en: A criticism of the government was implicit in his speech.
sentences.az: Onun çıxışında hökumətin tənqidi üstüörtülü şəkildə duyulurdu.

usage: EXPLICIT means stated clearly and in detail, leaving nothing to be guessed: explicit instructions, an explicit warning. It also describes books and films that show sex or violence openly. Its opposite, IMPLICIT, means suggested without being directly expressed; "implicit trust" means complete, unquestioning trust. In academic writing: "make an assumption explicit". Compare TACIT (understood without being said) and OVERT (done openly).

expressions.usage: Pattern: inhibit + object + FROM + -ing
shed = get rid of something that is not wanted
absorption = the process of taking a substance in
digestion = the process of changing food into substances the body can use
appetite = the desire for food
corrosion = the gradual destruction of metal by chemical action
release = the act of letting something out
dissent = disagreement with official opinions

sentences.en: Fear of failure can inhibit people from trying new things.
sentences.az: Uğursuzluq qorxusu insanların yeni şeyləri sınamasına mane ola bilər.

sentences.en: Tea can inhibit the absorption of iron.
sentences.az: Çay dəmirin mənimsənilməsini ləngidə bilər.

sentences.en: After a few minutes the children shed their inhibitions and began to sing.
sentences.az: Bir neçə dəqiqədən sonra uşaqlar sıxılmanı bir kənara qoyub oxumağa başladılar.

sentences.en: A special coating inhibits corrosion.
sentences.az: Xüsusi örtük korroziyanın qarşısını alır.

usage: INHIBIT means to prevent something from happening or developing normally, or to make somebody too nervous to act freely. It is common in science (inhibit growth, inhibit an enzyme) and in psychology. INHIBITIONS are feelings of embarrassment that stop you from behaving naturally: "lose / shed your inhibitions". Compare HINDER (make difficult), IMPEDE (delay progress) and PROHIBIT (forbid by rule) – "inhibit" never means "forbid".

expressions.usage: machinery = machines as a group
built-in = included as part of the design
factory = a building where goods are made
format = the way data is arranged or stored
hardware = the machinery and electronic parts of a computer
typewriter = a machine with keys for printing letters on paper
appliance = a machine for a particular task in the home
on the verge of = very near to the moment when something happens

sentences.en: The factory closed because its machinery was obsolete.
sentences.az: Zavod avadanlığı köhnəldiyi üçün bağlandı.

sentences.en: New technology has made many skills obsolete.
sentences.az: Yeni texnologiya bir çox bacarığı lazımsız edib.

sentences.en: Critics accuse phone makers of built-in obsolescence.
sentences.az: Tənqidçilər telefon istehsalçılarını məhsulların qəsdən tez köhnəldilməsində ittiham edirlər.

sentences.en: Cash is on the verge of obsolescence in some countries.
sentences.az: Bəzi ölkələrdə nağd pul istifadədən çıxmaq ərəfəsindədir.

usage: OBSOLETE means no longer used because something newer and better exists. The usual verbs are BECOME obsolete and MAKE or RENDER something obsolete. OUTDATED and OLD-FASHIONED describe things that are still in use but no longer modern; OBSOLETE is stronger. PLANNED (or BUILT-IN) OBSOLESCENCE is the practice of designing products so that they must soon be replaced – a frequent topic in essays on consumerism.

expressions.usage: disadvantage = something that causes problems
drawback = a disadvantage that makes something less attractive
downside = the negative part of a situation
pros and cons = the arguments for and against
inconvenience = trouble or difficulty
expense = the money that you spend on something
The passive pattern
vastly = very much

sentences.en: The advantages of the scheme far outweigh the disadvantages.
sentences.az: Layihənin üstünlükləri mənfi cəhətlərini qat-qat üstələyir.

sentences.en: In my view, the pros outweigh the cons.
sentences.az: Mənim fikrimcə, müsbət cəhətlər mənfiləri üstələyir.

sentences.en: Any savings are outweighed by the cost of transport.
sentences.az: İstənilən qənaət nəqliyyat xərci ilə üstələnir.

sentences.en: The benefits of exercise vastly outweigh the risks.
sentences.az: İdmanın faydaları risklərini qat-qat üstələyir.

usage: OUTWEIGH means to be greater or more important than something else. It is the key verb in one of the standard IELTS Task 2 questions: "Do the advantages outweigh the disadvantages?" It takes a direct object, with no preposition. Typical adverbs: far, greatly, vastly, clearly. Useful variations: "the benefits outweigh the costs", "the drawbacks are outweighed by the gains".

lessons.azerbaijani: qavramaq, dərk etmək; hesab etmək, ... kimi görmək

expressions.usage: Passive pattern + AS
depth = the distance from the front to the back, or from top to bottom
sensory = connected with the physical senses
distorted = changed so that it is no longer true or accurate
insult = a remark or action that offends somebody
snub = an action that ignores somebody deliberately
intuitively = by feeling rather than by reasoning
pause = a short period of silence or inactivity

sentences.en: The new tax is widely perceived as unfair.
sentences.az: Yeni vergi çoxları tərəfindən ədalətsiz hesab olunur.

sentences.en: Social media can give teenagers a distorted perception of reality.
sentences.az: Sosial media yeniyetmələrdə reallıq haqqında təhrif olunmuş təsəvvür yarada bilər.

sentences.en: There was a perceptible pause before she answered.
sentences.az: O, cavab verməzdən əvvəl sezilən fasilə oldu.

sentences.en: She made some very perceptive comments about the film.
sentences.az: O, film haqqında çox fərasətli fikirlər söylədi.

usage: PERCEIVE has two meanings: to notice or become aware of something ("perceive a change"), and to understand or think of something in a particular way ("be perceived AS a threat"). PERCEIVED before a noun means "believed to exist, whether or not it really does": a perceived threat, a perceived lack of support. PERCEPTION is how something is seen or understood: public perception. Spelling: "i before e except after c" – perCEIve.

expressions.usage: injustice = a situation that is not fair
fiction = something that is not true
oppression = cruel and unfair treatment of a group of people
ignorance = lack of knowledge
feud = an angry argument between two groups that lasts for years
segregation = the policy of separating groups of people
illusion = a false idea or belief
twilight = the faint light after sunset

sentences.en: Such films perpetuate harmful stereotypes about women.
sentences.az: Belə filmlər qadınlar haqqında zərərli stereotipləri yaşadır.

sentences.en: The current system perpetuates injustice.
sentences.az: Mövcud sistem ədalətsizliyi davam etdirir.

sentences.en: Advertising perpetuates the illusion that money brings happiness.
sentences.az: Reklam pulun xoşbəxtlik gətirdiyi illüziyasını yaşadır.

sentences.en: They lived in perpetual fear of being discovered.
sentences.az: Onlar aşkar edilmək qorxusu ilə daimi təşviş içində yaşayırdılar.

usage: PERPETUATE means to make a bad situation, belief or system continue for a long time: perpetuate a myth, a stereotype, inequality, the cycle of poverty. The object is nearly always negative. PERPETUAL describes something that continues without stopping or is repeated very often: perpetual noise. Do not confuse PERPETUATE with PERPETRATE (commit a crime: "perpetrate a fraud").

expressions.usage: concrete = a building material made from cement, sand and water
wall = a vertical structure of brick or stone
impression = an idea or feeling about what something is like
fence = a structure of wood or wire around a piece of land
conviction = a strong belief
border = the line that divides two countries
dam = a wall built across a river to hold back water
roof = the structure that covers the top of a building

sentences.en: The bridge is built of reinforced concrete.
sentences.az: Körpü dəmir-betondan tikilib.

sentences.en: The film reinforces the impression that crime is increasing.
sentences.az: Film cinayətkarlığın artdığı təəssüratını gücləndirir.

sentences.en: Engineers are working to reinforce the dam.
sentences.az: Mühəndislər bəndi möhkəmləndirmək üçün çalışırlar.

sentences.en: The experience reinforced my conviction that I had chosen the right career.
sentences.az: Bu təcrübə düzgün peşə seçdiyimə əminliyimi möhkəmləndirdi.

usage: REINFORCE means to make a structure stronger, or to make a feeling, idea or habit stronger: reinforce a belief, reinforce a stereotype, reinforce a message. In psychology, POSITIVE REINFORCEMENT is encouraging behaviour by rewarding it. REINFORCEMENTS (plural) are extra soldiers or police sent to help. Compare STRENGTHEN (general), BOLSTER (support and make stronger) and CONSOLIDATE (make a position more secure).

expressions.usage: persuasion = the act of making somebody agree to do something
frost = very cold weather when thin white ice forms
bribery = giving or taking money in exchange for dishonest help
decay = the process of being slowly destroyed by natural causes
depression = a medical condition of extreme sadness
manipulation = controlling people in a dishonest way
scam = a clever and dishonest plan for making money
genetically = in a way connected with genes

sentences.en: Young plants are susceptible to frost.
sentences.az: Cavan bitkilər şaxtaya davamsızdır.

sentences.en: Older people are more susceptible to scams.
sentences.az: Yaşlı insanlar fırıldaqlara daha asan aldanırlar.

sentences.en: Some people are genetically susceptible to the disease.
sentences.az: Bəzi insanlar bu xəstəliyə irsən meyillidirlər.

sentences.en: Teeth are susceptible to decay if they are not cleaned regularly.
sentences.az: Dişlər müntəzəm təmizlənməsə, çürüməyə meyilli olur.

usage: SUSCEPTIBLE means likely to be influenced, harmed or affected by something. It always takes TO: "susceptible TO infection / pressure / flattery". Compare VULNERABLE (weak and easily hurt), PRONE TO (likely to suffer from or to do something bad: prone to accidents) and LIABLE TO (likely to do something). Used alone of a person, it means easily influenced by feelings.

expressions.usage: The preposition is ABOUT
accountability = being responsible for your decisions and able to explain them
plastic = a light, strong material produced by chemical processes
fabric = cloth
liquid = a substance that flows freely, such as water
governance = the way an organisation or country is controlled
corporate = connected with a large company
ploy = a clever trick used to gain an advantage

sentences.en: The company should be more transparent about how it uses our data.
sentences.az: Şirkət məlumatlarımızdan necə istifadə etdiyi barədə daha açıq olmalıdır.

sentences.en: Voters are demanding greater transparency and accountability.
sentences.az: Seçicilər daha çox şəffaflıq və hesabatlılıq tələb edirlər.

sentences.en: The box is made of transparent plastic.
sentences.az: Qutu şəffaf plastikdən hazırlanıb.

sentences.en: His offer of help was a transparent ploy to win votes.
sentences.az: Onun kömək təklifi səs qazanmaq üçün açıq-aşkar hiylə idi.

usage: TRANSPARENT literally describes material that you can see through (compare OPAQUE, which you cannot). Of organisations it means open and honest, with nothing hidden: a transparent process. Of lies and excuses it means easy to recognise as false: "a transparent lie". TRANSPARENCY is a key word in essays on government and business, usually paired with ACCOUNTABILITY.

expressions.usage: division = a disagreement that separates people into groups
asthma = a medical condition that makes breathing difficult

expressions.az: kiminsə ağır vəziyyətini daha da pisləşdirmək
expressions.usage: plight = a difficult and sad situation
friction = disagreement between people with different opinions
rift = a serious break in a relationship
imbalance = a state in which two things are not equal
merely = only, and nothing more
acute = very serious or severe; a medical term

sentences.en: The drought has exacerbated the plight of farmers in the region.
sentences.az: Quraqlıq regiondakı fermerlərin ağır vəziyyətini daha da pisləşdirib.

sentences.en: Air pollution can exacerbate asthma.
sentences.az: Havanın çirklənməsi astmanı ağırlaşdıra bilər.

sentences.en: Higher interest rates would merely exacerbate the problem.
sentences.az: Faiz dərəcələrinin artırılması problemi yalnız daha da ağırlaşdırardı.

sentences.en: The minister's comments exacerbated divisions within the party.
sentences.az: Nazirin şərhləri partiya daxilindəki fikir ayrılıqlarını dərinləşdirdi.

usage: EXACERBATE means to make a bad situation, a problem or an illness worse. It is formal and typical of academic, medical and journalistic writing; its object is always something negative. Do not confuse it with EXASPERATE (annoy somebody very much) or EXAGGERATE (describe something as bigger than it is). Near synonyms: AGGRAVATE, WORSEN, COMPOUND, INFLAME. Opposites: ALLEVIATE, AMELIORATE, EASE.

expressions.usage: side-effect = an unwanted result of a drug or action
squalor = dirty and unpleasant living conditions
deprivation = not having the things necessary for a decent life
ordeal = a very difficult or painful experience
discomfort = slight pain or a feeling of being uncomfortable
shortcoming = a fault or weakness
trauma = a deeply upsetting experience

expressions.az: yaxşılaşdırmaq üçün çox az iş görmək
expressions.usage: Fixed pattern; "little" = almost nothing

sentences.en: The new housing programme is intended to ameliorate deprivation in inner cities.
sentences.az: Yeni mənzil proqramı şəhər mərkəzlərindəki məhrumiyyəti azaltmaq məqsədi daşıyır.

sentences.en: The drug can ameliorate the side-effects of the treatment.
sentences.az: Bu dərman müalicənin əlavə təsirlərini azalda bilər.

sentences.en: The reforms did little to ameliorate the situation.
sentences.az: İslahatlar vəziyyəti yaxşılaşdırmaq üçün çox az iş gördü.

sentences.en: Counselling helped to ameliorate the trauma of the survivors.
sentences.az: Psixoloji yardım sağ qalanların sarsıntısını yüngülləşdirməyə kömək etdi.

usage: AMELIORATE is a very formal verb meaning to make a bad or unpleasant situation better. It appears mainly in academic, legal and medical texts; in ordinary writing use IMPROVE or EASE. Its objects are negative conditions: poverty, suffering, conditions, effects. Compare ALLEVIATE (make suffering less severe) and MITIGATE (reduce the seriousness of harm). The direct opposite is EXACERBATE.

lessons.azerbaijani: hər yerdə rast gəlinən, hər yerə yayılmış

expressions.usage: presence = the fact of being in a place
surveillance = careful watching of people, especially by the police
smartphone = a mobile phone that works like a small computer

expressions.az: hər addımda rast gəlinən reklam lövhələri
expressions.usage: billboard = a large outdoor board for advertisements
graffiti = words or drawings on walls in public places
gadget = a small, clever device
jargon = technical words used by a particular group
Formal noun pattern

sentences.en: Smartphones have become ubiquitous in less than twenty years.
sentences.az: Smartfonlar iyirmi ildən az müddətdə hər yerə yayılıb.

sentences.en: Plastic is a ubiquitous presence in modern life.
sentences.az: Plastik müasir həyatda hər yerdə mövcuddur.

sentences.en: The ubiquity of social media has changed the way news travels.
sentences.az: Sosial medianın hər yerdə mövcudluğu xəbərlərin yayılma tərzini dəyişib.

sentences.en: Many people are worried about ubiquitous surveillance in city centres.
sentences.az: Bir çox insan şəhər mərkəzlərindəki hərtərəfli müşahidədən narahatdır.

usage: UBIQUITOUS means seeming to be everywhere. Because it begins with the sound /j/, it takes "a", not "an": "a ubiquitous feature". It is formal or humorous; neutral synonyms are WIDESPREAD and COMMON, while OMNIPRESENT is equally formal. It is very useful in essays on technology and advertising: "the ubiquitous mobile phone". Pronunciation: /juːˈbɪkwɪtəs/, with the stress on the second syllable.

lessons.azerbaijani: zərərli, məhvedici (xüsusilə gizli və tədrici şəkildə)

expressions.usage: myth = something that many people believe but that is not true
doctrine = a set of beliefs taught by a group
propaganda = false or one-sided information used to influence people
rumour = a piece of news that may not be true
legacy = a situation that exists because of past events
gossip = informal talk about other people's private lives
cycle = a series of events that repeat again and again
nonsense = ideas or statements that are not true or sensible

sentences.en: It is a pernicious myth that poor people do not want to work.
sentences.az: Yoxsulların işləmək istəməməsi zərərli bir mifdir.

sentences.en: The war left a pernicious legacy of hatred.
sentences.az: Müharibə özündən sonra nifrətdən ibarət ağır miras qoydu.

sentences.en: Poverty and poor health form a pernicious cycle.
sentences.az: Yoxsulluq və zəif sağlamlıq qapalı dövrə yaradır.

sentences.en: The article dismissed the theory as pernicious nonsense.
sentences.az: Məqalədə bu nəzəriyyə zərərli cəfəngiyat adlandırılaraq rədd edildi.

usage: PERNICIOUS describes something that has a very harmful effect, especially in a gradual way that is not easily noticed. It is a formal word of strong disapproval, used of ideas, influences and social practices rather than of physical objects: a pernicious influence, a pernicious effect. Compare INSIDIOUS (spreading secretly), DETRIMENTAL (harmful, neutral in tone) and MALIGN (evil in effect). "Pernicious anaemia" is a medical term.

expressions.usage: existence = a way of living, especially a difficult one
