foothold = a place for your foot when climbing; a secure starting position
ceasefire = an agreement to stop fighting
truce = an agreement between enemies to stop fighting for a time
equilibrium = a state of balance
perch = sit or rest on the edge of something
cling = hold on tightly
grip = a tight hold; control over something

sentences.en: Many families in the region lead a precarious existence.
sentences.az: Regiondakı bir çox ailə çətin dolanışıqla yaşayır.

sentences.en: The village is precariously perched on the edge of a cliff.
sentences.az: Kənd uçurumun kənarında güclə dayanıb.

sentences.en: The precarious ceasefire could collapse at any moment.
sentences.az: Kövrək atəşkəs istənilən an pozula bilər.

sentences.en: The president has only a precarious grip on power.
sentences.az: Prezidentin hakimiyyət üzərində nəzarəti zəifdir.

usage: PRECARIOUS describes a situation that is not safe or certain and could easily become worse, or an object that is likely to fall. It is common with FINANCIAL, POSITION and BALANCE: "a precarious financial position". "Precarious work" (insecure, badly paid jobs) is a current topic in sociology and economics. Do not confuse it with PRECIOUS (valuable). Synonyms: INSECURE, UNSTABLE, SHAKY (informal).

expressions.usage: nuclear = using the energy produced by splitting atoms
weapon = an object used for fighting, such as a gun or bomb
cell = the smallest unit of living matter
bacteria = very small living things, some of which cause disease
misinformation = wrong information, especially when it deceives people
exponentially = at a faster and faster rate
curb = control or limit something harmful
halt = stop

sentences.en: Fast-food restaurants have proliferated in the city centre.
sentences.az: Şəhərin mərkəzində fast-fud restoranları sürətlə çoxalıb.

sentences.en: The treaty aims to curb nuclear proliferation.
sentences.az: Müqavilənin məqsədi nüvə silahının yayılmasını cilovlamaqdır.

sentences.en: Bacteria proliferate rapidly in warm, damp conditions.
sentences.az: Bakteriyalar isti və rütubətli şəraitdə sürətlə çoxalır.

sentences.en: Social networks have accelerated the proliferation of misinformation.
sentences.az: Sosial şəbəkələr yanlış məlumatların yayılmasını sürətləndirib.

usage: PROLIFERATE means to increase rapidly in number or amount. It is intransitive: "Websites have proliferated" – you do not "proliferate something". The noun PROLIFERATION is strongly associated with weapons ("nuclear proliferation", "the Non-Proliferation Treaty"), but it is used for anything that multiplies quickly: the proliferation of mobile apps. Synonyms: MULTIPLY, MUSHROOM (informal), SPREAD.

lessons.azerbaijani: haqlı olduğunu sübut etmək, bəraət qazandırmaq

expressions.usage: Passive pattern: be vindicated by events
stance = an opinion that is stated publicly
judgement = the ability to make sensible decisions
the accused = the person on trial for a crime
appeal = a formal request to a higher court to change a decision
triumphant = very successful in a way that causes great satisfaction
suspicion = a feeling that something is wrong
instinct = a natural feeling that makes you act in a certain way

sentences.en: The court's decision completely vindicated her.
sentences.az: Məhkəmənin qərarı ona tam bəraət qazandırdı.

sentences.en: He felt vindicated by the results of the inquiry.
sentences.az: O, araşdırmanın nəticələri ilə haqlı çıxdığını hiss etdi.

sentences.en: The success of the film vindicated the director's judgement.
sentences.az: Filmin uğuru rejissorun mülahizəsinin düzgünlüyünü təsdiqlədi.

sentences.en: She saw the verdict as a triumphant vindication of her campaign.
sentences.az: O, hökmü öz kampaniyasının parlaq təsdiqi kimi qiymətləndirdi.

usage: VINDICATE means to prove that somebody was right, or that they are not guilty, after a period of doubt or criticism. It is often passive: "She has been vindicated." Objects: a person, a decision, a policy, a belief. Do not confuse it with VINDICTIVE (wanting revenge) – the two words are unrelated in meaning. Compare JUSTIFY (show to be reasonable), EXONERATE and ACQUIT (declare officially not guilty).

lessons.azerbaijani: yan keçmək, (qanunu və ya maneəni) dolanıb keçmək

expressions.usage: regulation = an official rule
obstacle = something that blocks your way
censorship = official control of what may be published
embargo = an official order that forbids trade with a country
bureaucracy = a complicated system of official rules
tariff = a tax on goods coming into a country
safeguard = a rule or measure that protects against harm
veto = the right to refuse to allow a decision

sentences.en: Some companies moved abroad to circumvent the new regulations.
sentences.az: Bəzi şirkətlər yeni qaydalardan yan keçmək üçün xaricə köçdü.

sentences.en: Users found ways to circumvent internet censorship.
sentences.az: İstifadəçilər internet senzurasından yan keçməyin yollarını tapdılar.

sentences.en: The goods were sent through a third country to circumvent the embargo.
sentences.az: Mallar embarqodan yan keçmək üçün üçüncü ölkə vasitəsilə göndərildi.

sentences.en: The government tried to circumvent parliament by using emergency powers.
sentences.az: Hökumət fövqəladə səlahiyyətlərdən istifadə edərək parlamentdən yan keçməyə çalışdı.

usage: CIRCUMVENT means to find a clever way of avoiding a rule, restriction or difficulty, without actually breaking the law. It often implies disapproval: circumvent the law, circumvent sanctions. Compare EVADE (escape something illegally: evade tax), BYPASS (go around; neutral) and GET ROUND (informal). Literally it can mean to travel around an obstacle. The Latin roots are "circum" (around) and "venire" (come).

expressions.usage: leaflet = a printed sheet of paper giving information
literature = here: printed information on a subject
expertise = special knowledge or skill
electronically = by means of computers
disinformation = false information spread deliberately
hatred = a very strong feeling of dislike
mass = involving a large number of people
journal = a serious magazine dealing with a specialised subject

sentences.en: The organisation disseminates information about healthy eating.
sentences.az: Təşkilat sağlam qidalanma haqqında məlumat yayır.

sentences.en: Research findings are usually disseminated through academic journals.
sentences.az: Tədqiqat nəticələri adətən elmi jurnallar vasitəsilə yayılır.

sentences.en: The report was disseminated electronically to all members.
sentences.az: Hesabat bütün üzvlərə elektron formada göndərildi.

sentences.en: Fake accounts were used to disseminate disinformation before the election.
sentences.az: Seçkidən əvvəl dezinformasiya yaymaq üçün saxta hesablardan istifadə olunub.

usage: DISSEMINATE means to spread information, knowledge or ideas so that they reach many people. It is formal and typical of academic and official language: disseminate information, findings, good practice. Compare SPREAD (general), CIRCULATE (pass from person to person), DISTRIBUTE (give out physical things) and PROPAGATE (spread ideas, often disapproving). The noun is common in research contexts: "the dissemination of results".

lessons.azerbaijani: təcəssüm etdirmək, ən parlaq nümunəsi olmaq

expressions.usage: elegance = the quality of being graceful and stylish
luxury = great comfort, especially with expensive things
sophistication = experience of the world and of fashion and culture
arrogance = behaving as if you are more important than others
glamour = the attractive and exciting quality of a person or place

expressions.az: nəyinsə ən yaxşı cəhətlərini təcəssüm etdirmək
expressions.usage: virtue = a good quality

expressions.az: dilemmanı ən parlaq şəkildə əks etdirmək
expressions.usage: dilemma = a situation in which a difficult choice must be made
zeitgeist = the general mood of a particular period (from German)

sentences.en: With her simple black dress, she was the epitome of elegance.
sentences.az: Sadə qara paltarı ilə o, zərifliyin təcəssümü idi.

sentences.en: The hotel is the epitome of luxury.
sentences.az: Bu mehmanxana dəbdəbənin təcəssümüdür.

sentences.en: His career epitomises the virtues of hard work and patience.
sentences.az: Onun karyerası zəhmətkeşlik və səbrin ən yaxşı cəhətlərini təcəssüm etdirir.

sentences.en: The band epitomised the zeitgeist of the 1960s.
sentences.az: Bu qrup 1960-cı illərin ruhunu təcəssüm etdirirdi.

usage: EPITOMISE (American: epitomize) means to be a perfect example of something. The noun EPITOME has four syllables and the final "e" is pronounced: /ɪˈpɪtəmi/ – a very common pronunciation mistake. The fixed pattern is "the epitome OF + abstract noun": the epitome of good taste, the epitome of evil. Synonyms: EMBODY, TYPIFY, EXEMPLIFY, PERSONIFY.

expressions.usage: action = the process of doing something; pattern: galvanise INTO
nation = a country and its people
voter = a person who has the right to vote
opposition = the political parties that are not in government
troops = soldiers, especially in large numbers
volunteer = a person who offers to do something without being paid
grassroots = the ordinary people in an organisation, not its leaders
steel = a strong metal made from iron

sentences.en: The shocking report galvanised the government into action.
sentences.az: Sarsıdıcı hesabat hökuməti hərəkətə keçməyə sövq etdi.

sentences.en: The speech galvanised voters across the country.
sentences.az: Bu çıxış bütün ölkədə seçiciləri hərəkətə gətirdi.

sentences.en: The disaster galvanised thousands of volunteers.
sentences.az: Fəlakət minlərlə könüllünü səfərbər etdi.

sentences.en: The roof is made of galvanised steel.
sentences.az: Dam sinklənmiş poladdan hazırlanıb.

usage: GALVANISE (American: galvanize) means to shock or excite people so that they take action. The usual patterns are "galvanise somebody INTO action / INTO doing something" and "galvanise support / opinion". In its technical sense it means to cover metal with zinc to protect it from rust. The word comes from the Italian scientist Luigi Galvani. Synonyms: SPUR, ROUSE, STIR, MOBILISE.

expressions.usage: juxtapose A WITH B
image = a picture or photograph
contrasting = very different; texture = the way a surface feels
comedy = a funny play or film; tragedy = a very sad event or play
quotation = words taken from a book or speech
jarring = unpleasantly different from what is around it
incongruous = strange because it does not suit the situation
bizarre = very strange

sentences.en: The exhibition juxtaposes modern paintings with medieval sculptures.
sentences.az: Sərgidə müasir rəsmlər orta əsr heykəlləri ilə yanaşı qoyulub.

sentences.en: The director juxtaposes images of wealth and poverty.
sentences.az: Rejissor var-dövlət və yoxsulluq təsvirlərini yanaşı qoyur.

sentences.en: The play juxtaposes comedy and tragedy in the same scene.
sentences.az: Pyesdə komediya və faciə eyni səhnədə qarşılaşdırılır.

sentences.en: There is a jarring juxtaposition of glass towers and wooden huts.
sentences.az: Şüşə göydələnlərlə taxta daxmaların göz deşən təzadı var.

usage: JUXTAPOSE means to put two different things side by side, especially to show a contrast or create an interesting effect. It is a key term for analysing art, film and literature: "The author juxtaposes past and present." The noun JUXTAPOSITION is at least as common as the verb: "the juxtaposition OF two ideas". Compare CONTRAST (show differences) and COMPARE (examine similarities and differences).

expressions.usage: portrayal = the way a person or thing is shown in a film or book
critique = a detailed analysis and judgement of something
perspective = a particular way of thinking about something
linguistic = connected with language
tone = the quality of a voice or the general character of writing
grasp = understand completely
appreciate = recognise the good qualities of
capture = succeed in representing accurately

sentences.en: The film offers a nuanced portrayal of life in a small town.
sentences.az: Film kiçik şəhərdəki həyatın incə çalarlı təsvirini verir.

sentences.en: It takes years to grasp the nuances of a foreign language.
sentences.az: Xarici dilin incəliklərini qavramaq illər tələb edir.

sentences.en: A good translation captures the nuances of the original.
sentences.az: Yaxşı tərcümə orijinalın çalarlarını əks etdirir.

sentences.en: The debate needs a more nuanced perspective.
sentences.az: Müzakirəyə daha incə çalarlı baxış lazımdır.

usage: A NUANCE is a very slight difference in meaning, sound, colour or feeling. NUANCED is a term of praise for analysis that recognises complexity instead of presenting things as black and white: "a nuanced argument". It is valuable in IELTS and academic discussion when you want to say that an issue is not simple. Pronunciation: /ˈnjuːɑːns/. Compare SUBTLETY (the quality of being subtle) and SHADE (a slightly different form of something).

lessons.azerbaijani: (adətən cəmdə) nəticə, fəsad, uzağa gedən təsir

expressions.usage: Usually plural: the ramifications OF a decision
unforeseen = not expected
diplomatic = connected with relations between countries
geopolitical = connected with the effect of geography on world politics
wide-ranging = covering many subjects or areas
dire = extremely serious or terrible
ponder = think carefully about something for a long time
ecological = connected with the relation of living things to their environment

sentences.en: Nobody fully understood the ramifications of the decision.
sentences.az: Heç kim bu qərarın nəticələrini tam dərk etmirdi.

sentences.en: The discovery could have wide-ranging ramifications for medicine.
sentences.az: Bu kəşfin tibb üçün genişmiqyaslı nəticələri ola bilər.

sentences.en: The crisis had unforeseen ramifications for the whole region.
sentences.az: Böhranın bütün region üçün qabaqcadan görülməyən nəticələri oldu.

sentences.en: Building the dam would have dire ecological ramifications.
sentences.az: Bəndin tikilməsinin ağır ekoloji nəticələri olardı.

usage: RAMIFICATIONS (nearly always plural) are the many complicated and unexpected results that follow an action or decision. The image is of branches spreading from a tree (Latin "ramus" = branch). It is more formal than CONSEQUENCES and stresses that the results are numerous and difficult to predict. Patterns: the ramifications OF something FOR somebody. Near synonyms: REPERCUSSIONS (usually negative), IMPLICATIONS (possible effects).

expressions.usage: inflammatory = intended to make people angry
populist = claiming to represent ordinary people against the elite
empty = here: with no meaning or value
reality = the true situation
device = a method of producing a particular effect
flourish = an impressive but unnecessary way of saying something
purely = only; completely
escalate = make something more intense

sentences.en: There is a wide gap between the government's rhetoric and reality.
sentences.az: Hökumətin sözü ilə əməli arasında böyük uçurum var.

sentences.en: Voters are tired of empty rhetoric.
sentences.az: Seçicilər içi boş sözlərdən yorulublar.

sentences.en: Repetition is a common rhetorical device in political speeches.
sentences.az: Təkrar siyasi çıxışlarda geniş yayılmış ritorik fənddir.

sentences.en: "Who cares?" is a rhetorical question: no answer is expected.
sentences.az: "Kimin vecinədir?" ritorik sualdır: cavab gözlənilmir.

usage: RHETORIC is the art of speaking or writing persuasively; in modern use it often means impressive language that is not sincere or is not followed by action ("empty rhetoric"). The noun is stressed on the first syllable (RHEtoric), the adjective on the second (rheTORical). A RHETORICAL QUESTION is asked for effect, not to get an answer. The "h" is silent.

expressions.usage: condemnation = a statement of very strong disapproval
rejection = the act of refusing to accept something
assurance = a promise that something is true or will happen
declaration = an official statement
pledge = a serious promise
mandate = the authority given to a government by the voters
affirm = state firmly that something is true
Verb + ON a subject

sentences.en: The attack drew unequivocal condemnation from world leaders.
sentences.az: Hücum dünya liderləri tərəfindən qəti şəkildə pislənildi.

sentences.en: The minister gave an unequivocal assurance that taxes would not rise.
sentences.az: Nazir vergilərin artmayacağına qəti təminat verdi.

sentences.en: The evidence is unequivocal: the climate is getting warmer.
sentences.az: Sübutlar birmənalıdır: iqlim istiləşir.

sentences.en: When asked about his plans, he equivocated.
sentences.az: Planları barədə soruşulanda o, qəti cavabdan yayındı.

usage: UNEQUIVOCAL means expressing an opinion or intention so clearly that there can be no doubt: unequivocal support, an unequivocal answer. It is stronger and more formal than CLEAR. EQUIVOCAL is its opposite: deliberately unclear, or difficult to interpret. To EQUIVOCATE is to avoid giving a direct answer. Compare UNAMBIGUOUS (having only one possible meaning) and CATEGORICAL (stated without any doubt).

expressions.usage: The usual pattern: the conundrum of how to ...
thorny = causing difficulty or disagreement
intriguing = very interesting because it is unusual
perplexing = difficult to understand
age-old = having existed for a very long time
grapple with = try hard to solve
unravel = explain something that is difficult to understand
insoluble = that cannot be solved

sentences.en: Governments face the conundrum of how to cut emissions without harming the economy.
sentences.az: Hökumətlər iqtisadiyyata ziyan vurmadan tullantıları necə azaltmaq müəmması ilə üzləşirlər.

sentences.en: Scientists are still grappling with this conundrum.
sentences.az: Alimlər hələ də bu müəmma ilə əlləşirlər.

sentences.en: How to care for an ageing population is a thorny conundrum.
sentences.az: Qocalan əhaliyə necə qulluq etmək çətin məsələdir.

sentences.en: It is an age-old conundrum: which came first, the chicken or the egg?
sentences.az: Bu, əzəli müəmmadır: əvvəl toyuq yaranıb, yoxsa yumurta?

usage: A CONUNDRUM is a confusing problem that is very difficult to solve, often because every solution creates a new difficulty. It is more colourful than PROBLEM and less emotional than DILEMMA, which is a choice between two unpleasant options. It can also mean a riddle with a clever answer. Typical verbs: face, pose, solve, resolve, grapple with a conundrum. The plural is CONUNDRUMS.

expressions.usage: panacea FOR a problem
universal = affecting everyone or everything

expressions.az: guya hər dərdin dərmanı sayılan vasitə
expressions.usage: supposed = believed by many, but perhaps wrongly
hardly = almost not
hail = describe publicly as very good
so-called = showing that you think the name is wrong
single = only one

expressions.az: sehrli həll yolu (bir zərbə ilə hər şeyi həll edən vasitə)
expressions.usage: silver = a shiny grey-white metal; bullet = a small metal object fired from a gun; idiom

sentences.en: Technology is not a panacea for all the problems of education.
sentences.az: Texnologiya təhsilin bütün problemlərinin universal çarəsi deyil.

sentences.en: The new drug was hailed as a panacea, but the results were disappointing.
sentences.az: Yeni dərman hər dərdin dərmanı kimi alqışlandı, amma nəticələr məyusedici oldu.

sentences.en: There is no single panacea for unemployment.
sentences.az: İşsizliyin vahid universal çarəsi yoxdur.

sentences.en: Lower taxes are useful, but they are hardly a panacea.
sentences.az: Aşağı vergilər faydalıdır, amma heç də universal çarə deyil.

usage: A PANACEA is something that is supposed to solve all problems or cure all illnesses. In practice it is nearly always used in the negative or with scepticism: "not a panacea", "no panacea", "a supposed panacea". This makes it ideal for a balanced conclusion in an IELTS essay: "Although X would help, it is no panacea." Informal equivalents are "a cure-all", "a magic bullet" and "a silver bullet". Stress: panaCEa.

lessons.azerbaijani: dixotomiya, iki əks qütbə bölünmə, kəskin ziddiyyət

expressions.usage: dichotomy BETWEEN A and B
rigid = very strict and difficult to change
fundamental = basic and very important
nature-nurture = inherited qualities versus upbringing
crude = simple and not accurate
transcend = go beyond the usual limits of
artificial = created by people; not natural or real
misleading = giving the wrong idea

sentences.en: There is often a dichotomy between what politicians say and what they do.
sentences.az: Siyasətçilərin dedikləri ilə etdikləri arasında çox vaxt kəskin ziddiyyət olur.

sentences.en: The dichotomy between work and play is an artificial one.
sentences.az: İşlə əyləncə arasındakı bölgü sünidir.

sentences.en: Modern research has moved beyond the nature-nurture dichotomy.
sentences.az: Müasir tədqiqatlar irsiyyət və tərbiyə qarşıdurmasından kənara çıxıb.

sentences.en: Dividing people into winners and losers is a crude dichotomy.
sentences.az: İnsanları qaliblərə və uduzanlara bölmək kobud bölgüdür.

usage: A DICHOTOMY is a division into two groups or ideas that are completely different or opposed. The standard pattern is "the dichotomy BETWEEN A and B". A FALSE DICHOTOMY is a logical fallacy: presenting two options as the only ones when others exist – a useful criticism in argumentative writing. Pronunciation: /daɪˈkɒtəmi/, with "ch" as /k/. Compare CONTRAST (a clear difference) and POLARITY (the state of having two opposite tendencies).

expressions.usage: dominant = more important or powerful than the others
Fixed prepositional pattern
existing = found or used now
classical = traditional and long-established
reigning = being the most important at present; from "reign"
overturn = reverse officially or completely
holistic = considering the whole of something, not just its parts
outdated = no longer useful because of being old

sentences.en: The discovery overturned the dominant paradigm in physics.
sentences.az: Bu kəşf fizikada hakim paradiqmanı alt-üst etdi.

sentences.en: The internet has caused a paradigm shift in the way we communicate.
sentences.az: İnternet ünsiyyət tərzimizdə paradiqma dəyişikliyinə səbəb olub.

sentences.en: Critics argue that the school system is based on an outdated paradigm.
sentences.az: Tənqidçilər iddia edirlər ki, məktəb sistemi köhnəlmiş paradiqmaya əsaslanır.

sentences.en: Most scientists work within the existing paradigm.
sentences.az: Alimlərin əksəriyyəti mövcud paradiqma çərçivəsində işləyir.

usage: A PARADIGM is a typical model or pattern, and especially the set of ideas and assumptions that a scientific community shares at a particular time. The famous phrase PARADIGM SHIFT (a fundamental change in approach) comes from the philosopher Thomas Kuhn. The "g" is silent: /ˈpærədaɪm/; but it is pronounced in the adjective PARADIGMATIC /ˌpærədɪɡˈmætɪk/. In grammar, a paradigm is a table of all the forms of a word.

expressions.usage: The preposition is ABOUT
smug = too pleased with yourself
guard against = take care to prevent
afford = be able to do something without risk; usually negative
breed = be the cause of
shatter = destroy completely
lull = make somebody feel safe when they are not
drift = move slowly without a clear purpose

sentences.en: We cannot afford to be complacent about road safety.
sentences.az: Yol təhlükəsizliyi məsələsində arxayınlaşmağa haqqımız yoxdur.

sentences.en: Success can breed complacency.
sentences.az: Uğur arxayınçılıq doğura bilər.

sentences.en: The defeat shattered the team's complacency.
sentences.az: Məğlubiyyət komandanın arxayınçılığını darmadağın etdi.

sentences.en: Low inflation lulled the government into complacency.
sentences.az: Aşağı inflyasiya hökuməti arxayın saldı.

usage: COMPLACENT means too satisfied with yourself or with a situation, so that you do not see the need for effort or change. It is always a criticism. Do not confuse it with COMPLAISANT (willing to please others), which is rare. The warning "There is no room for complacency" is a fixed formula in reports. Compare SMUG (irritatingly pleased with yourself) and SELF-SATISFIED.

expressions.usage: clause = a section of a legal document
amendment = a change made to a law or document
referendum = a vote in which all the people decide a question
merger = the joining of two companies into one
be in contention for a prize
Verb + WITH a difficulty
title = the position of champion
genuine = real, sincere

sentences.en: Immigration remains a contentious subject.
sentences.az: İmmiqrasiya mübahisəli mövzu olaraq qalır.

sentences.en: The most contentious clause in the treaty was removed.
sentences.az: Müqavilədəki ən mübahisəli bənd çıxarıldı.

sentences.en: Farmers have to contend with unpredictable weather.
sentences.az: Fermerlər gözlənilməz hava şəraiti ilə mübarizə aparmalı olurlar.

sentences.en: Three teams are still in contention for the title.
sentences.az: Üç komanda hələ də titul uğrunda mübarizədədir.

usage: CONTENTIOUS means likely to cause disagreement (a contentious issue) or, of a person, fond of arguing. It is close to CONTROVERSIAL but more formal. The verb CONTEND has three patterns: contend THAT (argue that something is true), contend WITH (deal with a difficulty) and contend FOR (compete for). "A bone of contention" is an idiom for a subject that people keep arguing about.

expressions.usage: The preposition is TO
merit = the quality of being good and deserving praise
reward = something given or gained for effort
extrinsic = coming from outside; the standard opposite
charm = the power of pleasing or attracting people
attribute = a quality or feature
worthwhile = important or useful enough to be worth the effort
intertwined = very closely connected

sentences.en: Small villages have an intrinsic charm that tourists love.
sentences.az: Kiçik kəndlərin turistlərin sevdiyi özünəməxsus cazibəsi var.

sentences.en: Flexibility is intrinsic to creative thought.
sentences.az: Çeviklik yaradıcı düşüncənin ayrılmaz hissəsidir.

sentences.en: Learning should be seen as intrinsically worthwhile.
sentences.az: Öyrənmək öz-özlüyündə dəyərli bir iş kimi qəbul edilməlidir.

sentences.en: Health and happiness are intrinsically intertwined.
sentences.az: Sağlamlıq və xoşbəxtlik bir-biri ilə ayrılmaz şəkildə bağlıdır.

usage: INTRINSIC describes a quality that belongs to the real nature of a thing: intrinsic value, intrinsic interest. In psychology, INTRINSIC MOTIVATION is doing something because it is enjoyable in itself, while EXTRINSIC motivation depends on rewards such as money or grades – a distinction worth knowing for IELTS topics on work and education. Compare INHERENT (existing as a natural, permanent part) and ESSENTIAL (necessary).

lessons.azerbaijani: son dərəcə dəqiq, vasvası, hər xırdalığa diqqət yetirən

expressions.usage: meticulous ABOUT / IN something
craftsman = a skilled person who makes things by hand
precision = the quality of being exact
reconstruction = building or forming something again
observation = the act of watching carefully
bookkeeping = keeping a record of the money a business spends and receives
groom = make yourself or an animal clean and neat
rehearse = practise a play or speech before performing it

sentences.en: She is meticulous about her appearance.
sentences.az: O, xarici görünüşünə son dərəcə diqqətlidir.

sentences.en: The trip was planned with meticulous precision.
sentences.az: Səfər zərgər dəqiqliyi ilə planlaşdırılmışdı.

sentences.en: The book is based on years of meticulous observation.
sentences.az: Kitab illərlə aparılmış diqqətli müşahidələrə əsaslanır.

sentences.en: Every detail of the ceremony had been meticulously rehearsed.
sentences.az: Mərasimin hər təfərrüatı diqqətlə məşq edilmişdi.

usage: METICULOUS means paying careful attention to every detail. It is a word of praise, unlike FUSSY or PEDANTIC, which suggest too much attention to unimportant details. Typical nouns: planning, research, preparation, attention to detail, records. Patterns: meticulous ABOUT / IN something. Synonyms: THOROUGH, SCRUPULOUS, PAINSTAKING, FASTIDIOUS. The adverb is extremely common before past participles: meticulously planned, meticulously researched.

lessons.azerbaijani: hər yerə nüfuz edən, geniş yayılmış

expressions.usage: atmosphere = the feeling or mood in a place
odour = a smell, especially an unpleasant one
theme = the main subject or idea
cynicism = the belief that people act only out of self-interest
apathy = lack of interest or enthusiasm
gloom = a feeling of sadness and hopelessness
novel = a long written story
discourse = serious discussion of a subject

sentences.en: There was a pervasive atmosphere of fear in the city.
sentences.az: Şəhərdə hər yeri bürümüş qorxu ab-havası var idi.

sentences.en: A sense of loss pervades the whole novel.
sentences.az: İtki hissi bütün romanın ruhuna hopub.

sentences.en: Loneliness is a pervasive theme in her poetry.
sentences.az: Tənhalıq onun poeziyasında hər yerdə duyulan mövzudur.

sentences.en: The influence of advertising is all-pervasive.
sentences.az: Reklamın təsiri hər şeyi bürüyüb.

usage: PERVASIVE describes something, often unpleasant, that spreads through every part of a place or thing: a pervasive smell, a pervasive influence, pervasive corruption. The verb PERVADE takes a direct object: "A smell of smoke pervaded the house." Compare PREVALENT (very common at a particular time or place) and UBIQUITOUS (seeming to be everywhere). ALL-PERVASIVE is an emphatic form.

expressions.usage: tribute = an act or statement showing respect or admiration
farewell = the act of saying goodbye
symbol = a thing that represents an idea
tale = a story
plea = an urgent and emotional request
reunion = a meeting of people who have been apart
Fixed comparative pattern: all the more + adjective
evoke = bring a feeling or memory into the mind

sentences.en: The empty chair was a poignant symbol of their loss.
sentences.az: Boş stul onların itkisinin təsirli rəmzi idi.

sentences.en: The film is a poignant tale of friendship in wartime.
sentences.az: Film müharibə dövründəki dostluq haqqında kövrək hekayətdir.

sentences.en: The fact that he died so young makes the story all the more poignant.
sentences.az: Onun bu qədər gənc ölməsi hekayəni daha da təsirli edir.

sentences.en: The novel poignantly evokes the author's childhood in Shusha.
sentences.az: Roman müəllifin Şuşadakı uşaqlığını ürəyə toxunan şəkildə canlandırır.

usage: POIGNANT means causing a sharp feeling of sadness or regret, often mixed with tenderness. The "g" is silent: /ˈpɔɪnjənt/. The classic collocation is "a poignant reminder OF something". It is a literary word, useful for reviewing books and films. Compare MOVING (causing deep feeling, not necessarily sad), TOUCHING (causing gentle sympathy) and HEARTBREAKING (causing extreme sadness).

lessons.azerbaijani: dirçəliş, yenidən canlanma, yenidən baş qaldırma

expressions.usage: resurgence IN / OF something
nationalism = the belief that your nation is better than others
virus = a very small living thing that causes infectious disease
measles = an infectious disease causing red spots on the skin
optimism = the feeling that good things will happen

expressions.az: dəniz quldurluğunun (və ya piratçılığın) yenidən artması
expressions.usage: piracy = attacking ships at sea; also illegal copying
unlikely = not expected to happen
dollar = the unit of money in the USA and other countries

sentences.en: There has been a resurgence of interest in traditional music.
sentences.az: Ənənəvi musiqiyə marağın yenidən canlanması müşahidə olunur.

sentences.en: Doctors are worried about a resurgence of measles.
sentences.az: Həkimlər qızılcanın yenidən yayılmasından narahatdırlar.

sentences.en: Vinyl records have enjoyed an unlikely resurgence.
sentences.az: Vinil vallar gözlənilməz dirçəliş yaşayıb.

sentences.en: A resurgent dollar has made imports cheaper.
sentences.az: Yenidən güclənən dollar idxalı ucuzlaşdırıb.

usage: A RESURGENCE is a return to growth, activity or popularity after a quiet period. It is singular and is followed by OF or IN: "a resurgence of violence", "a resurgence in demand". It can describe good and bad things alike. RESURGENT is the adjective: "resurgent nationalism". Compare REVIVAL (becoming popular or active again), COMEBACK (informal) and RENAISSANCE (a new period of interest in art or ideas).

expressions.usage: thread = a thin string; a connection between ideas
alliance = an agreement between countries or groups to work together
coalition = a government formed by several parties
bond = something that unites people
analogy = a comparison showing a similarity
basis = the facts or ideas from which something develops
parallel = a similar feature
premise = a statement on which reasoning is based

sentences.en: The link between the two events is tenuous at best.
sentences.az: Bu iki hadisə arasındakı əlaqə ən yaxşı halda zəifdir.

sentences.en: The government is held together by a tenuous coalition.
sentences.az: Hökumət zəif koalisiya ilə ayaqda durur.

sentences.en: The whole argument rests on a tenuous premise.
sentences.az: Bütün dəlil zəif ilkin müddəaya əsaslanır.

sentences.en: He has only a tenuous grasp of the facts.
sentences.az: Onun faktlardan anlayışı çox zəifdir.

usage: TENUOUS describes a connection, idea or situation that is weak and could easily be broken or shown to be false. The classic collocations are "a tenuous link / connection" and "a tenuous hold / grip ON something". "Tenuous at best" is a common critical phrase in essays. Compare FLIMSY (difficult to believe: a flimsy excuse), SHAKY and FRAGILE. Literally, tenuous means extremely thin.

lessons.azerbaijani: məkrli, gizli şəkildə zərər vuran, sinsi

expressions.usage: onset = the beginning of something unpleasant
enemy = a person or thing that wants to harm you
poison = a substance that causes death or harm
cancer = a serious disease in which cells grow uncontrollably
agenda = the hidden intention behind what somebody does
undercurrent = a hidden feeling whose effects are felt
flattery = praise that is not sincere
menace = a thing likely to cause serious harm

sentences.en: High blood pressure is an insidious disease with few symptoms.
sentences.az: Yüksək qan təzyiqi az simptomu olan sinsi xəstəlikdir.

sentences.en: The disease has an insidious onset.
sentences.az: Bu xəstəlik hiss olunmadan başlayır.

sentences.en: Corruption is an insidious cancer in public life.
sentences.az: Korrupsiya ictimai həyatda sinsi xərçəngdir.

sentences.en: There was an insidious undercurrent of racism in his remarks.
sentences.az: Onun sözlərində gizli irqçilik meyli duyulurdu.

usage: INSIDIOUS describes something harmful that spreads gradually and secretly, so that the damage is done before anyone notices. It is used of diseases, influences, habits and social problems: an insidious effect, the insidious spread of something. Do not confuse it with INVIDIOUS (unfair and likely to cause resentment: an invidious position). Compare PERNICIOUS (very harmful), STEALTHY (done quietly and secretly) and TREACHEROUS.

lessons.azerbaijani: imkan verməmək, istisna etmək, qarşısını almaq

expressions.usage: possibility = a thing that may happen
Pattern: preclude + object + FROM + -ing
The frequent negative form
prosecution = the process of charging somebody with a crime in court
disclosure = making secret information known
diagnosis = the identification of an illness
necessarily = in every case; usually in the negative
reconciliation = the ending of a disagreement

sentences.en: His injury precluded him from taking part in the final.
sentences.az: Zədəsi onun finalda iştirakına imkan vermədi.

sentences.en: The agreement does not preclude further talks.
sentences.az: Saziş sonrakı danışıqları istisna etmir.

sentences.en: Lack of evidence precluded prosecution.
sentences.az: Sübutların çatışmazlığı cinayət təqibini istisna etdi.

sentences.en: Being cautious does not necessarily preclude being ambitious.
sentences.az: Ehtiyatlı olmaq mütləq iddialı olmağı istisna etmir.

usage: PRECLUDE is a formal verb meaning to prevent something from happening or to make it impossible. Patterns: preclude something; preclude somebody FROM doing something. It is typical of legal and academic English and is very frequent in the negative: "This does not preclude ...". Compare PREVENT (general), RULE OUT (decide that something is not possible) and PROHIBIT (forbid by law).

expressions.usage: temptation = a strong wish to do something that you should not do
exhaustion = the state of being extremely tired
despair = the feeling of having lost all hope
fatigue = great tiredness
wound = an injury, especially a cut made by a weapon
lure = the attractive qualities of something
blackmail = demanding money by threatening to reveal secrets
eventually = at the end of a long period

sentences.en: He finally succumbed to temptation and had a second piece of cake.
sentences.az: O, nəhayət nəfsinə uydu və ikinci tort dilimini yedi.

sentences.en: The soldier succumbed to his wounds two days later.
sentences.az: Əsgər iki gün sonra aldığı yaralardan öldü.

sentences.en: Many young people succumb to the lure of the big city.
sentences.az: Bir çox gənc böyük şəhərin cazibəsinə tab gətirmir.

sentences.en: After hours of questioning, she eventually succumbed to pressure.
sentences.az: Saatlarla sorğu-sualdan sonra o, nəhayət təzyiqə təslim oldu.

usage: SUCCUMB is always followed by TO: succumb to pressure, to temptation, to an illness. It means to stop resisting something stronger than you; with illnesses and injuries it is a formal way of saying "die from": "She succumbed to cancer." The final "b" is silent: /səˈkʌm/. Synonyms: GIVE IN, YIELD, SURRENDER. The opposite is RESIST or WITHSTAND.

lessons.azerbaijani: bərabər, eyni gücə malik (mənfi bir şeyə)

expressions.usage: treason = the crime of betraying your country
murder = the crime of killing somebody deliberately
admission = a statement that something bad is true
surrender = the act of admitting defeat
betrayal = the act of not being loyal
torture = causing severe pain as a punishment
negligence = failure to give enough care or attention
sabotage = deliberate damage to prevent success

sentences.en: His silence was tantamount to an admission of guilt.
sentences.az: Onun susması günahını etiraf etməyə bərabər idi.

sentences.en: Leaving the patient without help would be tantamount to negligence.
sentences.az: Xəstəni köməksiz qoymaq səhlənkarlığa bərabər olardı.

sentences.en: For many fans, selling the club was tantamount to betrayal.
sentences.az: Bir çox azarkeş üçün klubu satmaq satqınlığa bərabər idi.

sentences.en: Criticising the leader was considered tantamount to treason.
sentences.az: Rəhbəri tənqid etmək xəyanətə bərabər sayılırdı.

usage: TANTAMOUNT is used only in the pattern "be tantamount TO something" and never before a noun. It means having the same bad effect as something else: the second thing is always negative (a lie, a threat, a crime). It is formal and typical of legal and political argument. Compare EQUIVALENT TO (neutral: equal in value or meaning) and AMOUNT TO (verb: "This amounts to a refusal").

lessons.azerbaijani: əsasını təşkil etmək, dayaq olmaq, möhkəmləndirmək

expressions.usage: rationale = the reasons for a decision or belief
curriculum = the subjects taught in a school or course
constitution = the basic laws of a country
ethos = the moral ideas and attitudes of a group
tenet = one of the principles on which a belief is based
notion = an idea or belief
empirical = based on experiments or experience rather than theory
solid = strong and reliable

sentences.en: The report is underpinned by extensive research.
sentences.az: Hesabat geniş tədqiqatlara əsaslanır.

sentences.en: Equality is the principle that underpins the constitution.
sentences.az: Bərabərlik konstitusiyanın əsasını təşkil edən prinsipdir.

sentences.en: The theory lacks any empirical underpinning.
sentences.az: Nəzəriyyənin heç bir empirik əsası yoxdur.

sentences.en: Trust underpins the whole ethos of the school.
sentences.az: Etimad məktəbin bütün dəyərlər sisteminin əsasında durur.

usage: UNDERPIN means to support or form the basis of an argument, claim or system: "the assumptions that underpin the theory". It is often passive: "be underpinned BY evidence". Literally, builders underpin a wall by putting a stronger support under it. The noun UNDERPINNING is often plural: "the theoretical underpinnings of the policy". Compare UNDERLIE (be the hidden cause or basis of) and SUPPORT (general).

expressions.usage: difficulty = a problem; a thing that is hard to do
peril = serious danger (literary)
complication = a thing that makes a situation more difficult
pitfall = a hidden danger or difficulty
encounter = a meeting, especially an unexpected or unpleasant one
marriage = the legal relationship between a husband and wife
frustration = the feeling of being annoyed because you cannot achieve something
paradox = a situation with two opposite features that seems strange

sentences.en: The journey across the mountains was fraught with peril.
sentences.az: Dağları aşan yol təhlükə ilə dolu idi.

sentences.en: Any attempt to reform the system is fraught with difficulty.
sentences.az: Sistemi islah etmək üçün istənilən cəhd çətinliklərlə doludur.

sentences.en: Buying a house abroad is fraught with pitfalls.
sentences.az: Xaricdə ev almaq gizli təhlükələrlə doludur.

sentences.en: Their marriage was fraught from the start.
sentences.az: Onların evliliyi əvvəldən gərgin idi.

usage: FRAUGHT has two uses. 1) FRAUGHT WITH + something unpleasant = full of it: fraught with danger, risk, problems, tension. 2) On its own (mainly British English) it means causing or feeling worry and stress: "a fraught situation", "She looked fraught." It is never followed by a positive noun. Pronunciation: /frɔːt/, rhyming with "caught". Compare TENSE (nervous) and RIDDLED WITH (full of something bad).

expressions.usage: impetus FOR a change / FOR reform
behind = being the cause of
lend = here: give a quality to something
inject = add a quality to something
original = existing at the beginning
tremendous = very great
much-needed = that is wanted very much
derive = get something from a source

sentences.en: The crisis provided the impetus for reform.
sentences.az: Böhran islahat üçün təkan verdi.

sentences.en: The new evidence lent fresh impetus to the investigation.
sentences.az: Yeni sübutlar istintaqa təzə təkan verdi.

sentences.en: The prize gave a tremendous impetus to her career.
sentences.az: Mükafat onun karyerasına çox güclü təkan verdi.

sentences.en: The movement derived its impetus from student protests.
sentences.az: Hərəkat təkanını tələbə etirazlarından alırdı.

usage: IMPETUS is something that makes a process happen, or happen more quickly. It is usually singular or uncountable and takes FOR, BEHIND or TO: "the impetus for change", "give impetus to the talks". Typical verbs: give, provide, lend, add, gain, lose impetus. Compare MOMENTUM (the force that keeps a process going once it has started), STIMULUS (something that causes a reaction) and INCENTIVE (a reward that encourages action).

expressions.usage: The preposition is IN
elite = a small group with a lot of power
privilege = a special advantage that only some people have
monopoly = complete control of trade in particular goods
hierarchy = a system in which people are ranked by importance
mindset = a fixed set of attitudes
Reflexive use of the verb
stalemate = a situation in which neither side can win

sentences.en: Sexism is deeply entrenched in our society.
sentences.az: Seksizm cəmiyyətimizdə dərin kök salıb.

sentences.en: The reforms threatened an entrenched elite.
sentences.az: İslahatlar möhkəmlənmiş elitanı təhdid edirdi.

sentences.en: It is hard to change such an entrenched mindset.
sentences.az: Belə dəyişməz düşüncə tərzini dəyişmək çətindir.

sentences.en: The new rules will only entrench the stalemate.
sentences.az: Yeni qaydalar çıxılmaz vəziyyəti yalnız daha da möhkəmləndirəcək.

usage: ENTRENCHED describes attitudes, habits or power that have existed for so long that they are very difficult to change. It is usually negative: deeply entrenched, firmly entrenched. The image is military: soldiers "entrench" themselves by digging trenches to defend a position. "Entrenched interests" are powerful groups that resist reform. Compare INGRAINED (of habits and beliefs) and DEEP-ROOTED or DEEP-SEATED.

expressions.usage: defence = protection against attack
ego = your sense of your own value and importance
courage = the ability to do something dangerous without showing fear
pride = a feeling of satisfaction in your achievements
immunity = the body's ability to resist disease
liquidity = the availability of cash in a business or market
turnout = the number of people who vote in an election
output = the amount of something produced

sentences.en: The victory bolstered the team's confidence.
sentences.az: Qələbə komandanın özünə inamını gücləndirdi.

sentences.en: The country is bolstering its defences along the border.
sentences.az: Ölkə sərhəd boyunca müdafiəsini gücləndirir.

sentences.en: A healthy diet helps to bolster immunity.
sentences.az: Sağlam qidalanma immuniteti gücləndirməyə kömək edir.

sentences.en: The central bank acted to bolster liquidity in the financial system.
sentences.az: Mərkəzi bank maliyyə sistemində likvidliyi artırmaq üçün tədbir gördü.

usage: BOLSTER means to improve something or make it stronger, especially confidence, an argument or an economy. It takes a direct object and is sometimes followed by UP: "bolster up the economy". Typical objects: confidence, morale, support, a claim, a position, the economy. As a noun, a bolster is a long firm pillow. Synonyms: STRENGTHEN, REINFORCE, BOOST, SHORE UP, BUTTRESS (formal).

expressions.usage: requirement = something that you must have or do
precaution = something done in advance to prevent problems
oversight = the responsibility for checking that work is done correctly
austerity = a situation in which a government spends as little as possible
protocol = a system of fixed rules for a procedure
supervision = watching a person or activity to make sure things are done correctly
compliance = the practice of obeying rules
Comparative pattern with "less"

sentences.en: Aircraft must meet stringent safety requirements.
sentences.az: Təyyarələr sərt təhlükəsizlik tələblərinə cavab verməlidir.

sentences.en: Stringent precautions were taken to prevent the spread of the virus.
sentences.az: Virusun yayılmasının qarşısını almaq üçün ciddi ehtiyat tədbirləri görüldü.

sentences.en: The rules for small companies are less stringent.
sentences.az: Kiçik şirkətlər üçün qaydalar daha az sərtdir.

sentences.en: Laboratories operate under stringent protocols.
sentences.az: Laboratoriyalar sərt protokollar əsasında fəaliyyət göstərir.

usage: STRINGENT describes rules, laws and standards that are very strict and must be obeyed: stringent regulations, controls, tests, standards. In economics it describes conditions in which there is little money: "stringent budgets". Compare STRICT (general), RIGOROUS (careful and thorough), TOUGH (informal) and DRACONIAN (extremely severe; disapproving). Opposites: LAX, LENIENT.

expressions.usage: highlight = emphasise; trait = a particular quality in a person's character
motif = a subject or idea that is repeated in a work of art
cue = a signal that helps you to understand or to act
landmark = a building or place that is easily recognised
passage = a short section of a book or speech
anecdote = a short, interesting story about a real event
variable = a factor that can change in an experiment
Formal noun pattern

sentences.en: The report summarises the salient points of the debate.
sentences.az: Hesabatda müzakirənin ən mühüm məqamları ümumiləşdirilir.

sentences.en: I have marked the salient passages in red.
sentences.az: Ən mühüm parçaları qırmızı ilə işarələmişəm.

sentences.en: The tower is the most salient landmark in the old town.
sentences.az: Qüllə köhnə şəhərdə ən çox seçilən oriyentirdir.

sentences.en: The salience of immigration as a political issue has increased.
sentences.az: İmmiqrasiyanın siyasi məsələ kimi aktuallığı artıb.

usage: SALIENT means most noticeable or important. It is formal and usually comes before the noun: the salient points, the salient features, the salient facts. "The salient features" is exactly what the IELTS Writing Task 1 instruction asks you to report ("selecting and reporting the main features"). Compare PROMINENT (easily seen; important), STRIKING (unusual enough to attract attention) and PERTINENT (directly relevant).

expressions.az: kimin və ya nəyinsə üçün nəticələri olmaq
expressions.usage: repercussions FOR somebody / ON something
grave = very serious and worrying
widespread = existing over a large area
catastrophic = causing a great deal of damage or suffering
devastating = causing severe shock or destruction
adverse = harmful or unfavourable
reverberate = have a strong, lasting effect; literally, echo
dread = be very afraid of something that may happen

sentences.en: The collapse of the bank had repercussions for the whole economy.
sentences.az: Bankın iflasının bütün iqtisadiyyat üçün nəticələri oldu.

sentences.en: Any delay could have grave repercussions.
sentences.az: İstənilən gecikmənin ağır nəticələri ola bilər.

sentences.en: The repercussions of the scandal reverberated for years.
sentences.az: Qalmaqalın nəticələri illərlə özünü göstərdi.

sentences.en: Cutting the health budget would have adverse repercussions for patients.
sentences.az: Səhiyyə büdcəsinin azaldılmasının xəstələr üçün mənfi nəticələri olardı.

usage: REPERCUSSIONS (usually plural) are the indirect and usually bad results of an action or event, which may continue for a long time. Patterns: repercussions FOR somebody; repercussions ON something; the repercussions OF an event. It is stronger and more negative than CONSEQUENCES. Compare RAMIFICATIONS (complex results that are hard to predict), AFTERMATH (the period after a disaster) and FALLOUT (the bad results of a situation).

expressions.usage: historical = connected with the past
apparent = seeming to be real, but perhaps not
strange = unusual or surprising
arise = begin to exist
congenital = existing from birth
spot = notice
rectify = put right something that is wrong
iron out = remove small problems; an iron is a tool for making clothes smooth

sentences.en: The results contained an anomaly that nobody could explain.
sentences.az: Nəticələrdə heç kimin izah edə bilmədiyi bir anomaliya var idi.

sentences.en: It is a historical anomaly that the two villages have different tax rules.
sentences.az: İki kəndin fərqli vergi qaydalarına malik olması tarixi anomaliyadır.

sentences.en: The software is designed to spot anomalies in bank accounts.
sentences.az: Proqram bank hesablarındakı uyğunsuzluqları sezmək üçün nəzərdə tutulub.

sentences.en: The new law will rectify this anomaly.
sentences.az: Yeni qanun bu uyğunsuzluğu aradan qaldıracaq.

usage: An ANOMALY is something that is different from what is normal or expected: an anomaly IN the data, an anomaly IN the system. It is common in science, statistics and law. ANOMALOUS is the adjective: "an anomalous result". Compare IRREGULARITY (something that does not follow the rules), ABERRATION (a temporary departure from what is normal) and OUTLIER (a value far from the others in a set of data).

expressions.usage: detention = the state of being kept in prison
threshold = the level at which something starts to happen
cut-off = a point or limit at which something stops
dismissal = the act of removing somebody from a job
punishment = a penalty for doing something wrong
whim = a sudden wish to do something unusual
assign = give somebody a task or put them in a group
category = a group of things with similar features

sentences.en: The choice of forty as the pass mark seems arbitrary.
sentences.az: Keçid balı kimi qırxın seçilməsi əsassız görünür.

sentences.en: Human rights groups condemned the arbitrary detention of journalists.
sentences.az: Hüquq müdafiə təşkilatları jurnalistlərin özbaşına həbsini pislədi.

sentences.en: Students were arbitrarily assigned to one of three groups.
sentences.az: Tələbələr təsadüfi qaydada üç qrupdan birinə təyin edildi.

sentences.en: The law protects employees against arbitrary dismissal.
sentences.az: Qanun işçiləri əsassız işdən çıxarılmadan qoruyur.

usage: ARBITRARY describes a decision or rule that is not based on a reason, system or plan and therefore often seems unfair. In law and politics it means using power without restriction: arbitrary arrest, arbitrary rule. Do not confuse it with ARBITRATION (settling a dispute through an independent person). Compare RANDOM (without any pattern), CAPRICIOUS (changing suddenly) and DISCRETIONARY (decided by somebody's judgement).

expressions.usage: romance = a love affair
sector = a part of a country's economic activity
metropolis = a very large and important city
deficit = the amount by which spending is greater than income
export = a product sold to another country
empire = a group of countries or companies controlled by one ruler or owner
workload = the amount of work that has to be done
burgeon INTO something larger

sentences.en: Baku is a burgeoning metropolis on the Caspian Sea.
sentences.az: Bakı Xəzər dənizi sahilində sürətlə böyüyən nəhəng şəhərdir.

sentences.en: The country has a burgeoning technology sector.
sentences.az: Ölkənin sürətlə böyüyən texnologiya sektoru var.

sentences.en: The small business burgeoned into an international company.
sentences.az: Kiçik müəssisə böyüyüb beynəlxalq şirkətə çevrildi.

sentences.en: The government is struggling with a burgeoning deficit.
sentences.az: Hökumət sürətlə artan kəsirlə mübarizə aparır.

usage: BURGEON is a literary and journalistic verb meaning to begin to grow or develop rapidly. It is used far more often as the adjective BURGEONING before a noun: a burgeoning population, a burgeoning market, burgeoning demand. Originally it described plants putting out new buds. Synonyms: FLOURISH, THRIVE, BOOM, MUSHROOM. It is intransitive: things burgeon; you cannot "burgeon something".

expressions.usage: rebuttal = a statement that says a claim is false
thesis = a statement or opinion that is discussed logically
exposition = a full explanation of a theory or plan
synthesis = a combination of ideas into a whole
appraisal = a judgement of the value or quality of something
commentary = a written explanation or discussion of something
prose = writing that is not poetry
concise = giving only the necessary information in few words

sentences.en: She presented a cogent case for reform.
sentences.az: O, islahatın zəruriliyini tutarlı şəkildə əsaslandırdı.

sentences.en: The article offers a cogent rebuttal of the minister's claims.
sentences.az: Məqalədə nazirin iddialarının tutarlı təkzibi verilir.

sentences.en: A good essay is cogent and concise.
sentences.az: Yaxşı esse tutarlı və yığcam olur.

sentences.en: He argued his point cogently.
sentences.az: O, fikrini inandırıcı şəkildə əsaslandırdı.

usage: COGENT describes an argument, reason or piece of writing that is clear, logical and convincing. It is a term of praise in academic contexts: "a cogent argument", "cogent reasons". The "g" is soft: /ˈkəʊdʒənt/. Compare CONVINCING and PERSUASIVE (making you believe), COMPELLING (so strong that you must accept it) and COHERENT (logically connected, though not necessarily convincing).

expressions.usage: conflate A WITH B
A very common pattern
religion = belief in a god; ethnicity = belonging to a particular people
journalism = the work of reporting news; entertainment = films, shows and other amusements
equality = having the same rights; uniformity = being the same in every way
separate = different, not connected; phenomena = facts or events (singular: phenomenon)
incident = something that happens, especially something unpleasant
lazy = not making enough effort

sentences.en: People often conflate wealth with success.
sentences.az: İnsanlar çox vaxt var-dövləti uğurla eyniləşdirirlər.

sentences.en: Privacy and secrecy are different things; we should not conflate the two.
sentences.az: Şəxsi həyatın toxunulmazlığı ilə gizlilik fərqli şeylərdir; bu ikisini qarışdırmamalıyıq.

sentences.en: The witness seems to have conflated two incidents.
sentences.az: Deyəsən, şahid iki hadisəni bir-birinə qarışdırıb.

sentences.en: It is a mistake to conflate equality with uniformity.
sentences.az: Bərabərliyi eynilik ilə qarışdırmaq səhvdir.

usage: To CONFLATE is to combine two or more separate ideas, texts or sets of information into one, usually wrongly. It is a precise critical verb for essays: "The author conflates correlation with causation." Patterns: conflate A WITH / AND B; conflate the two. Compare CONFUSE (mistake one thing for another), EQUATE (treat as equal) and MERGE (join together, neutral).

expressions.usage: absence = the fact of not being present
display = an arrangement or show of something
bravery = the quality of being brave
exception = a thing that does not follow a rule
extravagance = spending more money than is necessary
omission = something that has not been included
tattoo = a picture marked permanently on the skin
doorway = the space where a door opens

sentences.en: The minister was conspicuous by his absence.
sentences.az: Nazirin yoxluğu dərhal gözə çarpırdı.

sentences.en: He was awarded a medal for conspicuous bravery.
sentences.az: O, xüsusi igidliyə görə medalla təltif olundu.

sentences.en: There is one conspicuous omission from the list.
sentences.az: Siyahıda bir gözə çarpan çatışmazlıq var.

sentences.en: The entrance is an inconspicuous doorway between two shops.
sentences.az: Giriş iki mağaza arasında gözə çarpmayan bir qapıdır.

usage: CONSPICUOUS means easy to see or notice, often because of being different. "Conspicuous by its / his absence" is a fixed ironic phrase: noticed because it is not there. CONSPICUOUS CONSUMPTION is buying expensive things in order to impress others – a term from sociology. The opposite is INCONSPICUOUS. Compare NOTICEABLE (easy to see), PROMINENT (important or well known) and OBTRUSIVE (noticeable in an unpleasant way).

expressions.usage: version = one person's description of an event
alibi = evidence that somebody was elsewhere when a crime happened
allegation = a statement, made without proof, that somebody has done wrong
assertion = a statement that you strongly believe is true
recollection = a memory of something
estimate = a judgement of size or cost made without exact figures
Formal fixed phrase
The frequent passive pattern

sentences.en: The evidence was corroborated by two independent witnesses.
sentences.az: Sübutlar iki müstəqil şahid tərəfindən təsdiqləndi.

sentences.en: Nobody could corroborate his alibi.
sentences.az: Heç kim onun alibisini təsdiq edə bilmədi.

sentences.en: The documents corroborate the allegations of fraud.
sentences.az: Sənədlər dələduzluq ittihamlarını təsdiq edir.

sentences.en: The court will not accept such a claim without corroboration.
sentences.az: Məhkəmə belə bir iddianı təsdiqedici sübut olmadan qəbul etməyəcək.

usage: CORROBORATE means to provide evidence that supports a statement, theory or account. It is formal and typical of legal and academic language; it is often passive: "be corroborated BY". Compare CONFIRM (show that something is definitely true), SUBSTANTIATE (provide proof for a claim), VERIFY (check that something is correct) and VALIDATE (show to be acceptable or correct).

expressions.usage: Always in this pattern: a dearth OF + noun
nurse = a person trained to care for sick people
imagination = the ability to form new ideas or pictures in your mind
rainfall = the amount of rain that falls
engineer = a person who designs machines, roads or bridges
amenity = a useful feature of a place, such as a shop or park
vacancy = a job that is available
chronic = lasting for a long time; difficult to cure

sentences.en: There is a dearth of reliable information on the subject.
sentences.az: Bu mövzuda etibarlı məlumat qıtlığı var.

sentences.en: Rural hospitals suffer from a chronic dearth of nurses.
sentences.az: Kənd xəstəxanaları tibb bacılarının xroniki çatışmazlığından əziyyət çəkir.

sentences.en: The new suburb has a dearth of amenities.
sentences.az: Yeni şəhərətrafı qəsəbədə məişət xidmətləri çatışmır.

sentences.en: A dearth of rainfall has ruined the harvest.
sentences.az: Yağıntı qıtlığı məhsulu məhv edib.

usage: DEARTH is a formal noun used almost only in the pattern "a dearth OF something", meaning that there is not enough of it. It is singular and takes a singular verb: "There is a dearth of evidence." Pronunciation: /dɜːθ/, rhyming with "earth". Compare LACK (general), SHORTAGE (not enough of something needed), SCARCITY (a situation in which something is hard to obtain) and PAUCITY (very formal). The opposite idea is PLETHORA or ABUNDANCE.

lessons.azerbaijani: dəqiq müəyyən etmək, sərhədini cızmaq; ətraflı təsvir etmək

expressions.usage: contour = the outer shape of something
zone = an area with a particular feature or use
parameter = a limit that controls how something should be done
jurisdiction = the authority to make legal decisions
frontier = a line that separates two countries
remit = the area of activity over which somebody has authority
perimeter = the outside edge of an area
Formal noun pattern

sentences.en: The contract clearly delineates the responsibilities of each partner.
sentences.az: Müqavilə hər bir tərəfdaşın məsuliyyətini aydın şəkildə müəyyən edir.

sentences.en: A white line delineates the perimeter of the pitch.
sentences.az: Ağ xətt meydançanın xarici sərhədini cızır.

sentences.en: The report delineates the parameters of the inquiry.
sentences.az: Hesabat araşdırmanın çərçivəsini müəyyən edir.

sentences.en: The treaty delineated the frontier between the two states.
sentences.az: Müqavilə iki dövlət arasındakı sərhədi müəyyən etdi.

usage: DELINEATE means to describe or mark something precisely, especially a boundary or a set of duties. It is formal: delineate responsibilities, delineate roles, delineate boundaries. It is frequently passive with an adverb: "clearly delineated", "sharply delineated". Compare OUTLINE (give the main points), DEMARCATE (mark the limits of an area) and DEFINE (state exactly what something is).

expressions.usage: mechanism = the way in which something works
pathway = a series of stages or reactions leading to a result
obscure = difficult to understand; verse = a line or group of lines of poetry
riddle = a question that is difficult to understand and has a clever answer
intricacy = one of the complicated details of something
dynamics = the way in which people or things react to each other
metaphor = a way of describing something by comparing it to something else
context = the situation in which something happens

sentences.en: The lecturer used a diagram to elucidate the mechanism.
sentences.az: Mühazirəçi mexanizmi aydınlaşdırmaq üçün sxemdən istifadə etdi.

sentences.en: Further research is needed to elucidate the dynamics of the process.
sentences.az: Prosesin dinamikasını aydınlaşdırmaq üçün əlavə tədqiqatlar lazımdır.

sentences.en: The notes elucidate the more obscure verses of the poem.
sentences.az: Qeydlər poemanın daha anlaşılmaz misralarını izah edir.

sentences.en: Could you elucidate your last point?
sentences.az: Son fikrinizi aydınlaşdıra bilərsinizmi?

usage: ELUCIDATE is a formal verb meaning to make something clear by explaining it more fully. It takes a direct object or stands alone: "Let me elucidate." It is typical of academic writing and scientific papers ("elucidate the mechanism"). Compare CLARIFY (make easier to understand), EXPLAIN (general) and ILLUMINATE (make clearer, often by giving new information). The root is the Latin "lucidus" (clear), as in LUCID.

expressions.usage: pleasure = a feeling of enjoyment
beauty = the quality of being pleasing to look at
glory = great honour and admiration
craze = an enthusiastic interest that lasts a short time
glimpse = a very brief look
fleeting = lasting only a short time
sculpture = a work of art made by shaping stone, metal or other material
thrill = a sudden strong feeling of excitement

sentences.en: Fame in the age of social media is ephemeral.
sentences.az: Sosial media dövründə şöhrət ötəridir.

sentences.en: The artist makes ephemeral sculptures out of ice and sand.
sentences.az: Rəssam buzdan və qumdan qısaömürlü heykəllər düzəldir.

sentences.en: Most online crazes are ephemeral.
sentences.az: İnternetdəki dəblərin çoxu ötəridir.

sentences.en: The poem is about the ephemeral beauty of spring flowers.
sentences.az: Şeir yaz çiçəklərinin keçici gözəlliyindən bəhs edir.

usage: EPHEMERAL means lasting for only a very short time. It is a literary and academic word, common in discussions of fashion, fame, media and art: "the ephemeral nature of fame". Pronunciation: /ɪˈfemərəl/ – "ph" is /f/. Compare TRANSIENT (staying or lasting only a short time), FLEETING (passing very quickly), SHORT-LIVED (plain English) and TEMPORARY (intended to last a limited time). The noun EPHEMERA means things that are used for a short time, such as tickets and posters.

expressions.usage: polio = a serious infectious disease that can cause paralysis
smallpox = a serious infectious disease, now eradicated
malaria = a disease caused by the bite of some mosquitoes
terrorism = the use of violence for political aims
slavery = the system of owning people as property
pest = an insect or animal that destroys plants or food
superstition = a belief that is not based on reason or science
scourge = something that causes great suffering

sentences.en: Smallpox was eradicated in 1980.
sentences.az: Çiçək xəstəliyinin kökü 1980-ci ildə kəsilib.

sentences.en: The campaign aims to eradicate polio worldwide.
sentences.az: Kampaniyanın məqsədi bütün dünyada poliomielitin kökünü kəsməkdir.

sentences.en: It will take decades to eradicate the scourge of corruption.
sentences.az: Korrupsiya bəlasının kökünü kəsmək onilliklər çəkəcək.

sentences.en: Farmers use chemicals to eradicate pests.
sentences.az: Fermerlər zərərvericiləri məhv etmək üçün kimyəvi maddələrdən istifadə edirlər.

usage: ERADICATE means to destroy or get rid of something bad completely: eradicate a disease, eradicate poverty, eradicate racism. It is stronger than REDUCE or TACKLE and suggests that nothing remains (Latin "radix" = root: to pull up by the roots). Compare ELIMINATE (remove completely; more general), WIPE OUT (informal) and STAMP OUT (end something bad by strong action). "Eradicate poverty" is a favourite collocation in IELTS essays.

expressions.usage: The usual pattern: the fallacy OF + noun / -ing
gambler = a person who risks money on games of chance
sunk-cost = money already spent that cannot be recovered

expressions.az: "saman müqəvva" yanılması (rəqibin fikrini təhrif edib təkzib etmək)
expressions.usage: straw-man = a weak, invented version of an opponent's argument
refute = prove that a statement is wrong
debunk = show that an idea or belief is false
enduring = lasting for a long time
inference = a conclusion reached from the facts available

sentences.en: It is a fallacy that money always brings happiness.
sentences.az: Pulun həmişə xoşbəxtlik gətirməsi yanlış təsəvvürdür.

sentences.en: Continuing a bad project because of the money already spent is the sunk-cost fallacy.
sentences.az: Artıq xərclənmiş pula görə uğursuz layihəni davam etdirmək batmış xərclər yanılmasıdır.

sentences.en: The book debunks several popular fallacies about diet.
sentences.az: Kitab pəhrizlə bağlı bir neçə geniş yayılmış yanlış fikri ifşa edir.

sentences.en: His conclusion rests on a fallacious inference.
sentences.az: Onun gəldiyi nəticə yanlış çıxarışa əsaslanır.

usage: A FALLACY is a false idea that many people believe, or an error in reasoning that makes an argument invalid. Naming fallacies is useful in critical essays: the STRAW-MAN fallacy (attacking a distorted version of the other side's view), the FALSE DICHOTOMY, the SLIPPERY SLOPE. FALLACIOUS is the formal adjective. Compare MISCONCEPTION (a wrong idea based on poor understanding) and MYTH (a widely held false belief).

expressions.usage: flow = the steady movement of something in one direction
The preposition is TO
circulation = the movement of blood, air or traffic around a system
breathing = the act of taking air into the lungs
navigation = the movement of ships; also finding the way
drainage = the system or process by which water flows away
pedestrian = a person who is walking in the street
formidable = very great and difficult to deal with

sentences.en: Fallen trees impeded the flow of traffic.
sentences.az: Yıxılmış ağaclar nəqliyyatın axınını ləngitdi.

sentences.en: Tight clothing can impede circulation.
sentences.az: Dar paltar qan dövranını ləngidə bilər.

sentences.en: The lack of funds is a formidable impediment to progress.
sentences.az: Vəsait çatışmazlığı irəliləyişə ciddi maneədir.

sentences.en: Cars parked on the pavement impede pedestrians.
sentences.az: Səkidə saxlanılan maşınlar piyadaların hərəkətinə mane olur.

usage: IMPEDE means to delay or stop the progress of something. It is more formal than HINDER and close to HAMPER and OBSTRUCT. The noun IMPEDIMENT takes TO: "an impediment to growth"; a "speech impediment" is a condition that makes it difficult to speak clearly. The Latin root means "to tie the feet" – compare PEDESTRIAN and PEDAL. Opposites: FACILITATE, EXPEDITE.

expressions.usage: countdown = the counting of seconds backwards to zero before an event
slide = a change to a lower or worse condition
tide = the regular rise and fall of the sea; also a strong movement of opinion
fate = the things that will happen to somebody and cannot be changed
descent = a movement downwards
climb = an increase in value or amount; also the act of going up
logic = a way of reasoning in which each step follows from the one before
Common adverbial pattern with verbs of movement

sentences.en: The inexorable rise in prices worries every family.
sentences.az: Qiymətlərin qarşısıalınmaz artımı hər bir ailəni narahat edir.

sentences.en: The country seemed to be moving inexorably towards war.
sentences.az: Ölkə sanki dönmədən müharibəyə doğru gedirdi.

sentences.en: The film traces the hero's inexorable descent into madness.
sentences.az: Film qəhrəmanın dəliliyə doğru qarşısıalınmaz enişini izləyir.

sentences.en: The inexorable logic of the market forced the smaller shops to close.
sentences.az: Bazarın dönməz məntiqi kiçik mağazaları bağlanmağa məcbur etdi.

usage: INEXORABLE describes a process that cannot be stopped or changed: the inexorable rise of prices, the inexorable march of time. It is formal and often used of trends in essays. The adverb INEXORABLY is at least as common: "move inexorably towards". Stress: inEXorable. Compare RELENTLESS (never stopping or becoming weaker), UNSTOPPABLE (plain English) and INEVITABLE (certain to happen).

expressions.usage: code = a set of instructions for a computer
paper = documents; trail = a series of marks or records left behind
blame = responsibility for something bad
wrongdoing = illegal or dishonest behaviour
smokescreen = something said or done to hide the truth
verbal = connected with words
wilful = done deliberately, although it is wrong
evade = avoid dealing with something

sentences.en: The minister was accused of trying to obfuscate the issue.
sentences.az: Nazir məsələni qəsdən dolaşdırmağa çalışmaqda ittiham olundu.

sentences.en: The company used complex accounting to obfuscate wrongdoing.
sentences.az: Şirkət qanunsuz əməli ört-basdır etmək üçün mürəkkəb mühasibat üsullarından istifadə etdi.

sentences.en: His answer was a masterpiece of verbal obfuscation.
sentences.az: Onun cavabı söz oyunu ilə çaşdırmanın şah əsəri idi.

sentences.en: Instead of answering, officials continued to obfuscate and evade.
sentences.az: Rəsmilər cavab vermək əvəzinə məsələni dolaşdırmaqda və yayınmaqda davam etdilər.

usage: OBFUSCATE means to make something unclear or difficult to understand, especially deliberately. It is a formal word of criticism for politicians, lawyers and bureaucrats who hide the truth behind complicated language. In computing, code is obfuscated to protect it from being copied. Compare OBSCURE (make difficult to see or understand), CONFUSE (general) and MUDDY THE WATERS (idiom). Opposites: CLARIFY, ELUCIDATE.

expressions.usage: Always in this pattern: a plethora OF + plural noun
app = a program for a phone or tablet
acronym = a word formed from the first letters of a name
website = a set of pages on the internet
committee = a group of people chosen to make decisions
platform = a type of computer system or online service
loophole = a mistake in a law that allows people to avoid obeying it
bewildering = confusing because there are too many things

sentences.en: There is a plethora of apps for learning languages.
sentences.az: Dil öyrənmək üçün çoxlu sayda tətbiq var.

sentences.en: Consumers face a bewildering plethora of choices.
sentences.az: İstehlakçılar baş gicəlləndirən seçim bolluğu ilə üzləşirlər.

sentences.en: The report is full of a plethora of acronyms.
sentences.az: Hesabat saysız-hesabsız abreviatura ilə doludur.

sentences.en: The tax code contains a plethora of loopholes.
sentences.az: Vergi məcəlləsində çoxlu sayda boşluq var.

usage: PLETHORA means a very large amount of something, strictly more than is needed, though in modern use it often simply means "a lot". The pattern is "a plethora OF + plural noun", usually with a plural verb in everyday English. Stress the first syllable: PLEthora /ˈpleθərə/. Compare ABUNDANCE (a large, welcome quantity), PROFUSION (a very large quantity), SURFEIT and GLUT (too much). The opposite is DEARTH.

expressions.usage: propensity FOR + noun
propensity + to-infinitive
exaggerate = make something seem larger or more important than it is
procrastinate = delay doing something that you should do
mischief = bad behaviour that is annoying but not serious
hoard = collect and keep large amounts of something
innate = that you have when you are born
conform = behave in the way that most other people do

sentences.en: He has a propensity to exaggerate.
sentences.az: Onun şişirtməyə meyli var.

sentences.en: Humans have an innate propensity for language.
sentences.az: İnsanların dilə anadangəlmə meyli var.

sentences.en: Students have a propensity to procrastinate before exams.
sentences.az: Tələbələrin imtahanlardan əvvəl işi təxirə salmağa meyli var.

sentences.en: People in crowds show a strong propensity to conform.
sentences.az: İzdiham içindəki insanlar çoxluğa uymağa güclü meyil göstərirlər.

usage: PROPENSITY is a formal noun for a natural tendency to behave in a particular way, often a bad one. Patterns: a propensity FOR something; a propensity TO do something. In economics, "the propensity to consume" is the proportion of income that people spend. Compare TENDENCY (general), INCLINATION (a feeling that makes you want to do something), PREDISPOSITION (a condition that makes something likely) and PENCHANT (a special liking).

adv.az: ən səciyyəvi şəkildə, tam mənası ilə

expressions.usage: gentleman = a man who is polite and behaves well
villain = the main bad character in a story
hero = a person admired for brave or good actions
pub = a building where people go to drink and meet friends
seaside = an area by the sea; resort = a place where people go on holiday

expressions.az: cəmiyyətdən kənarda qalan adamın tipik nümunəsi
expressions.usage: outsider = a person who is not accepted as a member of a group
underdog = a person or team thought to be in a weaker position
Formal noun pattern

sentences.en: He was the quintessential English gentleman.
sentences.az: O, əsl ingilis centlmeninin nümunəsi idi.

sentences.en: Brighton is the quintessential seaside resort.
sentences.az: Brayton tipik dənizkənarı kurortdur.

sentences.en: Tea with milk is quintessentially British.
sentences.az: Südlü çay tam mənası ilə Britaniyaya xasdır.

sentences.en: The film's hero is the quintessential outsider.
sentences.az: Filmin qəhrəmanı cəmiyyətdən kənarda qalan adamın tipik nümunəsidir.

usage: QUINTESSENTIAL means being the most typical or perfect example of a kind of person or thing: "the quintessential tourist". It always comes before a noun and usually follows "the". QUINTESSENTIALLY is common before nationalities: quintessentially English. The noun QUINTESSENCE means the perfect example or the most important feature: "the quintessence of good taste". Compare TYPICAL (plain), ARCHETYPAL (the original model) and CLASSIC.

expressions.usage: charge = an official claim that somebody has committed a crime
lawsuit = a claim brought to a court of law
signature = your name written in your own way
sentiment = a feeling or opinion, especially one based on emotion
invoice = a list of goods or services with the amount to be paid
credentials = documents that prove your qualifications
comparison = the act of examining similarities and differences
patently = clearly and without doubt

sentences.en: He was arrested on spurious charges.
sentences.az: O, əsassız ittihamlarla həbs olundu.

sentences.en: The company was fined for sending spurious invoices.
sentences.az: Şirkət saxta hesab-fakturalar göndərdiyinə görə cərimələndi.

sentences.en: The argument rests on a spurious comparison between the two countries.
sentences.az: Dəlil iki ölkə arasındakı əsassız müqayisəyə söykənir.

sentences.en: The claim that the drug cures cancer is patently spurious.
sentences.az: Bu dərmanın xərçəngi sağaltdığı iddiası açıq-aşkar əsassızdır.

usage: SPURIOUS means false, although seeming to be genuine, or based on false reasoning: a spurious argument, a spurious claim, spurious accuracy. In statistics, a SPURIOUS CORRELATION is a connection between two sets of figures that appears real but is caused by chance or by a third factor. Compare BOGUS (pretending to be real), FAKE (a copy), SPECIOUS (seeming right but actually wrong) and UNFOUNDED (not based on facts).
